spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m7p2t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS East, West, Kits, NoRead

VARIABLES reg, obs, shelf, reserved, opened

vars == <<reg, obs, shelf, reserved, opened>>

Wings == {East, West}

Stock == Cardinality(Kits)

\* Two independent wing schedulers share one sterile store. A reservation is a
\* compare-and-swap: the writer re-presents the value it read and writes back a
\* value derived from that reading, so a lost decrement would desynchronise the
\* advertised count from the shelf. StoreCoherent forbids exactly that drift.

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in 0..Stock
  /\ obs \in [Wings -> (0..Stock) \cup {NoRead}]
  /\ shelf \subseteq Kits
  /\ reserved \in [Wings -> SUBSET Kits]
  /\ opened \in [Wings -> SUBSET Kits]

Held(w) == reserved[w] \cup opened[w]

StoreCoherent ==
  /\ reg = Cardinality(shelf)
  /\ shelf \cup (UNION {Held(w) : w \in Wings}) = Kits
  /\ \A w \in Wings :
       /\ shelf \cap Held(w) = {}
       /\ reserved[w] \cap opened[w] = {}
  /\ \A v, w \in Wings : v # w => Held(v) \cap Held(w) = {}

Init ==
  /\ reg = Stock
  /\ obs = [w \in Wings |-> NoRead]
  /\ shelf = Kits
  /\ reserved = [w \in Wings |-> {}]
  /\ opened = [w \in Wings |-> {}]

Read(w) ==
  /\ obs[w] = NoRead
  /\ obs' = [obs EXCEPT ![w] = reg]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, shelf, reserved, opened>>

ClaimOK(w) ==
  /\ obs[w] # NoRead
  /\ obs[w] = reg
  /\ obs[w] > 0
  /\ shelf # {}
  /\ \E k \in shelf :
       /\ shelf' = shelf \ {k}
       /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![w] = reserved[w] \cup {k}]
  /\ reg' = obs[w] - 1
  /\ obs' = [obs EXCEPT ![w] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED opened

ClaimFail(w) ==
  /\ obs[w] # NoRead
  /\ (obs[w] # reg \/ shelf = {})
  /\ obs' = [obs EXCEPT ![w] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, shelf, reserved, opened>>

Open(w) ==
  /\ reserved[w] # {}
  /\ \E k \in reserved[w] :
       /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![w] = reserved[w] \ {k}]
       /\ opened' = [opened EXCEPT ![w] = opened[w] \cup {k}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, obs, shelf>>

Recycle(w) ==
  /\ opened[w] # {}
  /\ \E k \in opened[w] :
       /\ opened' = [opened EXCEPT ![w] = opened[w] \ {k}]
       /\ shelf' = shelf \cup {k}
  /\ reg' = reg + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<obs, reserved>>

Next == \E w \in Wings : Read(w) \/ ClaimOK(w) \/ ClaimFail(w) \/ Open(w) \/ Recycle(w)

AttemptResolves ==
  \A w \in Wings : (obs[w] # NoRead) ~> (obs[w] = NoRead)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ SF_vars(ClaimOK(East)) /\ SF_vars(ClaimFail(East)) /\ SF_vars(ClaimOK(West)) /\ SF_vars(ClaimFail(West))
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  East = east
  West = west
  Kits = {k1, k2, k3}
  NoRead = none
INVARIANT StoreCoherent
PROPERTY AttemptResolves
nl:
St. Auber's hospital runs two operating-room scheduling services, one for the east wing and one for the west wing. The two services were written by different teams and run on different machines; neither knows anything about the other. They do, however, draw sterile instrument kits from one single shared sterile store. Every kit in the hospital is a physical object: at any instant it is either sitting on the shelf in the store, or reserved by exactly one wing's scheduler, or opened on a table in exactly one wing's theatre, and it is never in two of those places and never nowhere.

Because the two services are independent, the store does not hand out kits with a mutex. Instead the store publishes a single shared register that advertises how many kits are currently on the shelf, and the schedulers coordinate through a compare-and-swap discipline. A scheduler that wants a kit first reads the register and remembers the number it saw. Later it attempts the swap: it re-presents the number it read, and the store only lets the reservation through if the register still holds exactly that number. When it does, the store hands over one shelf kit and the scheduler writes back the value it computed from its own reading, one less than what it saw. If in the meantime the other wing changed the register -- or if the shelf turned out to be empty -- the attempt is rejected, the scheduler forgets its reading, and it is free to read again and retry.

Reserved kits are later opened for a case, and kits opened in a theatre are eventually sent through the steriliser and come back to the shelf, at which point the store bumps the register up by one as it puts the kit back.

The danger the hospital is guarding against is not two surgeons fighting over one table. It is the register drifting away from physical reality: if both schedulers read the same number and both write back their own decrement, one decrement is lost and the register claims more kits are on the shelf than actually exist, or a kit gets accounted for twice. The compare-and-swap discipline exists precisely so that the advertised count and the physical whereabouts of every kit stay in agreement.

The full action set is: Read (a scheduler with no reading in hand samples the register), ClaimOK (a scheduler whose remembered reading still matches the register, with the shelf non-empty, takes one shelf kit into its reservations and writes back its remembered value minus one), ClaimFail (a scheduler whose remembered reading no longer matches, or which finds the shelf empty, discards its reading), Open (a scheduler moves one of its reserved kits onto a theatre table), Recycle (a kit on a theatre table is sterilised, returned to the shelf, and the register is bumped up by one).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every kit is at all times on the shelf, reserved by exactly one wing, or open in exactly one wing's theatre and never in two of those at once, and the shared register always states exactly how many kits are physically on the shelf.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every compare-and-swap attempt eventually resolves -- a scheduler that is holding a remembered reading of the register always eventually either completes its reservation or discards the reading, so no scheduler is left stuck mid-attempt forever.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m9p2t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Riders, CarCap, EpochLimit

VARIABLES epoch, carEpoch, onboard, atLobby, arrived, adminHold

vars == <<epoch, carEpoch, onboard, atLobby, arrived, adminHold>>

\* Epoch-numbered dispatch plans: a car works only while carEpoch[c] = epoch.
\* Resync and warden evacuation hand riders back rather than dropping them.
\* The guarded claim is that the three kinds of place always partition Riders.

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..EpochLimit
  /\ carEpoch \in [Cars -> 0..EpochLimit]
  /\ onboard \in [Cars -> SUBSET Riders]
  /\ atLobby \subseteq Riders
  /\ arrived \subseteq Riders
  /\ adminHold \in BOOLEAN

Carried == UNION {onboard[c] : c \in Cars}

RidersAccountedFor ==
  /\ atLobby \cup arrived \cup Carried = Riders
  /\ atLobby \cap arrived = {}
  /\ \A c \in Cars :
       /\ onboard[c] \cap atLobby = {}
       /\ onboard[c] \cap arrived = {}
  /\ \A a, b \in Cars : a # b => onboard[a] \cap onboard[b] = {}

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ carEpoch = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ onboard = [c \in Cars |-> {}]
  /\ atLobby = Riders
  /\ arrived = {}
  /\ adminHold = FALSE

Board(c, r) ==
  /\ ~adminHold
  /\ r \in atLobby
  /\ carEpoch[c] = epoch
  /\ Cardinality(onboard[c]) < CarCap
  /\ onboard' = [onboard EXCEPT ![c] = onboard[c] \cup {r}]
  /\ atLobby' = atLobby \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, carEpoch, arrived, adminHold>>

Deliver(c) ==
  /\ onboard[c] # {}
  /\ carEpoch[c] = epoch
  /\ arrived' = arrived \cup onboard[c]
  /\ onboard' = [onboard EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, carEpoch, atLobby, adminHold>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ ~adminHold
  /\ epoch < EpochLimit
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<carEpoch, onboard, atLobby, arrived, adminHold>>

Resync(c) ==
  /\ carEpoch[c] < epoch
  /\ carEpoch' = [carEpoch EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
  /\ atLobby' = atLobby \cup onboard[c]
  /\ onboard' = [onboard EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, arrived, adminHold>>

AssertHold ==
  /\ ~adminHold
  /\ adminHold' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, carEpoch, onboard, atLobby, arrived>>

Evacuate(c) ==
  /\ adminHold
  /\ onboard[c] # {}
  /\ atLobby' = atLobby \cup onboard[c]
  /\ onboard' = [onboard EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
  /\ carEpoch' = [carEpoch EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, arrived, adminHold>>

ReleaseHold ==
  /\ adminHold
  /\ \A c \in Cars : onboard[c] = {}
  /\ adminHold' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, carEpoch, onboard, atLobby, arrived>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars, r \in Riders : Board(c, r)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Deliver(c) \/ Resync(c) \/ Evacuate(c)
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ AssertHold
  \/ ReleaseHold

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Cars = {carA, carB}
  Riders = {p1, p2, p3}
  CarCap = 2
  EpochLimit = 2
INVARIANT RidersAccountedFor
nl:
Vertex Tower runs a bank of elevator cars serving a single sky-lobby. The bank controller publishes a dispatch plan, and every plan carries an epoch number. When traffic patterns change (morning rush, a floor closure, a fire drill rehearsal), the controller issues a reconfiguration: it bumps the bank epoch by one and the previous plan becomes stale. A car is only allowed to accept riders while the epoch stamped on the plan it is currently executing matches the bank epoch. A car running a stale plan has to resync before it may work again, and resyncing means it opens its doors at the sky-lobby and hands every rider it is currently carrying back to the lobby crowd, because those riders were routed under assumptions that no longer hold.

Riders enter the system in the sky-lobby. A car with a current plan and free space may board one waiting rider at a time, up to the car's rated occupancy. A car that is carrying riders and still has a current plan may complete its run, at which point the riders it carries are delivered and have arrived at their destinations; they never re-enter the lobby crowd.

The building also has a privileged admin override, used by the fire warden. The warden can place the bank on hold: while the hold is active no car may board riders and the controller may not issue any further reconfiguration. During a hold, the warden may evacuate any car, which returns every rider on that car to the lobby and also stamps that car with the current bank epoch. The warden may only release the hold once every car is empty.

The thing the tower's safety case cares about is that riders are neither invented nor misplaced by any of this churn. Boarding, delivery, resync and warden evacuation all move riders between exactly three kinds of place: the lobby crowd, the inside of exactly one car, and the arrived hall. Reconfiguration and holds move nobody at all. No rider may ever appear in two places at once, and no rider may ever vanish from all of them.

The full action set is: Board (a current-epoch car takes one lobby rider if under capacity and no hold is active), Deliver (a current-epoch car unloads its riders into the arrived hall), Reconfigure (the controller bumps the bank epoch, up to a limit, when no hold is active), Resync (a stale car adopts the bank epoch and returns its riders to the lobby), AdminHold (the warden asserts the hold), AdminEvacuate (during a hold, the warden empties one car back to the lobby and re-stamps its epoch), AdminRelease (the warden lifts the hold once all cars are empty).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every rider is at all times in exactly one of the lobby crowd, the interior of exactly one car, or the arrived hall -- the three kinds of location are pairwise disjoint and together always cover the entire rider population.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m9p6t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS TrainA, TrainB, Blocks, NoBlock, Vacant, EpochLimit

VARIABLES epoch, net, auth, authEp, occ

vars == <<epoch, net, auth, authEp, occ>>

Trains == {TrainA, TrainB}

\* Movement authorities carry the interlocking epoch; the radio delivers grants
\* in any order, so a superseded grant can surface late and must be refused.
\* CurrentAuthorityOnly is the guard that no stale grant is ever held by a train.

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..EpochLimit
  /\ net \subseteq (Trains \X Blocks \X (0..EpochLimit))
  /\ auth \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {NoBlock}]
  /\ authEp \in [Trains -> 0..EpochLimit]
  /\ occ \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {Vacant}]

CurrentAuthorityOnly == \A t \in Trains : auth[t] # NoBlock => authEp[t] = epoch

Promised(b) == \/ occ[b] # Vacant
               \/ \E t \in Trains : auth[t] = b
               \/ \E m \in net : m[2] = b

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ net = {}
  /\ auth = [t \in Trains |-> NoBlock]
  /\ authEp = [t \in Trains |-> 0]
  /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> Vacant]

Issue(t, b) ==
  /\ auth[t] = NoBlock
  /\ ~Promised(b)
  /\ net' = net \cup {<<t, b, epoch>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, auth, authEp, occ>>

Deliver(m) ==
  /\ m \in net
  /\ auth[m[1]] = NoBlock
  /\ m[3] = epoch
  /\ auth' = [auth EXCEPT ![m[1]] = m[2]]
  /\ authEp' = [authEp EXCEPT ![m[1]] = m[3]]
  /\ net' = net \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, occ>>

DiscardStale(m) ==
  /\ m \in net
  /\ m[3] < epoch
  /\ net' = net \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, auth, authEp, occ>>

Enter(t) ==
  /\ auth[t] # NoBlock
  /\ authEp[t] = epoch
  /\ occ[auth[t]] = Vacant
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![auth[t]] = t]
  /\ auth' = [auth EXCEPT ![t] = NoBlock]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, net, authEp>>

Leave(t) ==
  /\ \E b \in Blocks : occ[b] = t /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = Vacant]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, net, auth, authEp>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < EpochLimit
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ auth' = [t \in Trains |-> NoBlock]
  /\ authEp' = [t \in Trains |-> epoch + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<net, occ>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Issue(t, b)
  \/ \E m \in net : Deliver(m) \/ DiscardStale(m)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : Enter(t) \/ Leave(t)
  \/ Reconfigure

AuthorityConsumed == \A t \in Trains : (auth[t] # NoBlock) ~> (auth[t] = NoBlock)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ SF_vars(Enter(TrainA)) /\ SF_vars(Leave(TrainA)) /\ SF_vars(Enter(TrainB)) /\ SF_vars(Leave(TrainB))
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  TrainA = ta
  TrainB = tb
  Blocks = {bk1, bk2}
  NoBlock = noblock
  Vacant = vacant
  EpochLimit = 1
INVARIANT CurrentAuthorityOnly
PROPERTY AuthorityConsumed
nl:
The Line 4 subway is divided into signalling blocks. A train may only stand in a block if the interlocking has granted it a movement authority for that block. The interlocking is periodically reconfigured -- a track possession is opened, a points machine is swapped, a temporary speed restriction comes into force -- and every reconfiguration bumps the interlocking's epoch number by one. Every movement authority the interlocking issues is stamped with the epoch that was current when it was issued.

Authorities are sent to trains over the trackside radio, which does not preserve order. A grant sits in the radio network until a train picks it up, and grants may be picked up in any order, so a train can be offered an authority that was stamped several epochs ago while a fresher one is still in flight. A train will only take up an authority whose stamp equals the interlocking's current epoch; a grant carrying a superseded stamp is dropped from the network by the radio housekeeper rather than delivered. When the interlocking reconfigures, it revokes outright every authority that trains are currently holding but have not yet acted on, because those authorities were computed against a track layout that no longer exists.

A train holding a current authority for a vacant block moves into it, consuming the authority. A train standing in a block may leave it, freeing the block. To keep the radio traffic sane the interlocking will not issue a second authority for a block that is already occupied, already promised to a train that is holding an authority for it, or already the subject of an undelivered grant.

The point of the epoch stamping is that no stale actor gets to act. A train must never be found holding an authority that the interlocking has already superseded, however late or out of order the radio delivers things.

The full action set is: Issue (the interlocking puts an epoch-stamped grant for a vacant, unpromised block into the radio network for an idle train), Deliver (an idle train picks up any grant addressed to it from the network, but only if its stamp is the current epoch), DiscardStale (the radio housekeeper removes from the network any grant whose stamp has been superseded), Enter (a train holding a current authority moves into the named block if it is vacant, consuming the authority), Leave (a train standing in a block vacates it), Reconfigure (the interlocking bumps its epoch, up to a limit, and simultaneously revokes every authority currently held by a train).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No train ever holds a movement authority whose epoch stamp differs from the interlocking's current epoch -- every held authority is one the current configuration issued and has not superseded.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: An authority a train is holding is never held forever -- every authority a train takes up is eventually consumed by entering the named block or revoked by a reconfiguration, so no train sits indefinitely on an unspent authority.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m5p4t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Replicas, Applicants, Ceiling, InitialCap, RoundLimit

VARIABLES seated, cap, ballot, round, chairMoves

vars == <<seated, cap, ballot, round, chairMoves>>

\* One admission is decided per ballot round; overlapping majorities mean a round
\* has at most one winner. Replicas stop voting once the room is full, so the
\* seated students plus any standing winner can never outgrow the cap.

TypeOK ==
  /\ seated \subseteq Applicants
  /\ cap \in 0..Ceiling
  /\ ballot \in [Replicas -> Applicants \cup {"abstain"}]
  /\ round \in 0..RoundLimit
  /\ chairMoves \in 0..RoundLimit

VotesFor(a) == {r \in Replicas : ballot[r] = a}
Majority(a) == 2 * Cardinality(VotesFor(a)) > Cardinality(Replicas)
Winners == {a \in Applicants : Majority(a)}

NoOverAdmission == Cardinality(seated) + Cardinality(Winners) <= cap

Init ==
  /\ seated = {}
  /\ cap = InitialCap
  /\ ballot = [r \in Replicas |-> "abstain"]
  /\ round = 0
  /\ chairMoves = 0

Vote(r, a) ==
  /\ round < RoundLimit
  /\ ballot[r] = "abstain"
  /\ a \notin seated
  /\ Cardinality(seated) < cap
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![r] = a]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seated, cap, round, chairMoves>>

Seat(a) ==
  /\ Majority(a)
  /\ seated' = seated \cup {a}
  /\ ballot' = [r \in Replicas |-> "abstain"]
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, chairMoves>>

Abandon ==
  /\ \E r \in Replicas : ballot[r] # "abstain"
  /\ round < RoundLimit
  /\ ballot' = [r \in Replicas |-> "abstain"]
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seated, cap, chairMoves>>

ChairRaise ==
  /\ chairMoves < RoundLimit
  /\ cap < Ceiling
  /\ cap' = cap + 1
  /\ chairMoves' = chairMoves + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seated, ballot, round>>

ChairLower ==
  /\ chairMoves < RoundLimit
  /\ cap > Cardinality(seated) + Cardinality(Winners)
  /\ cap' = cap - 1
  /\ chairMoves' = chairMoves + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seated, ballot, round>>

ChairUnseat(a) ==
  /\ a \in seated
  /\ chairMoves < RoundLimit
  /\ seated' = seated \ {a}
  /\ chairMoves' = chairMoves + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, ballot, round>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Replicas, a \in Applicants : Vote(r, a)
  \/ \E a \in Applicants : Seat(a) \/ ChairUnseat(a)
  \/ Abandon
  \/ ChairRaise
  \/ ChairLower

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Replicas = {rep1, rep2, rep3}
  Applicants = {s1, s2, s3}
  Ceiling = 3
  InitialCap = 1
  RoundLimit = 3
INVARIANT NoOverAdmission
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
Northmoor University runs course registration through a small cluster of registrar replicas. A seat in a capped seminar is far too valuable to hand out on a single machine's say-so, so the cluster decides admissions one at a time, by ballot. There is a current ballot round; in that round each replica may cast its vote for at most one applicant. An applicant whose votes form a strict majority of the replicas is declared the winner of the round and is seated; seating a winner closes the round, clears every replica's vote, and opens the next round. Because a replica votes at most once per round and any two majorities overlap, at most one applicant can ever be the winner of a given round.

A replica will only cast a vote at all while the seminar still has room -- that is, while the number of students already seated is strictly below the current cap. If a round produces no majority, or the cluster simply wants to move on, the round can be abandoned: the votes are cleared and the round counter advances with nobody seated.

The department chair has a privileged override that bypasses the ballot entirely. The chair may raise the cap, up to a hard ceiling set by the fire code for the room. The chair may lower the cap again, but only down to the number of students currently seated, never below it. And the chair may unilaterally unseat a student, freeing room without any vote being taken.

What the registrar has to guarantee is that the room is never oversubscribed, and that includes promises already made but not yet written down: if some applicant has already gathered a majority in the open round, that applicant is effectively seated, so the seated students plus any such standing winner must still fit under the cap. A cluster that let replicas keep voting once the room was full would violate this even before the commit happened.

The full action set is: Vote (a replica that has not yet voted in this round casts its vote for an unseated applicant, permitted only while seated students are strictly under the cap and the round counter is below its limit), Seat (an applicant holding a strict majority in the open round is seated, the round closes, votes are cleared and the round counter advances), Abandon (the open round is discarded, votes are cleared and the round counter advances with nobody seated), ChairRaise (the chair raises the cap by one, up to the fire-code ceiling), ChairLower (the chair lowers the cap by one, never below the number of seated students), ChairUnseat (the chair removes a seated student).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of students already seated plus the number of applicants that have already gathered a majority of replica votes in the open round never exceeds the current cap.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m7p6t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS SorterA, SorterB, Bags, NoObs, NoWrite, TicketLimit, BookSize

VARIABLES reg, obs, ticket, outstanding, book

vars == <<reg, obs, ticket, outstanding, book>>

Sorters == {SorterA, SorterB}

\* Charge of the diverter is taken by compare-and-swap on a ticket register.
\* A slow sorter may wake up holding a superseded ticket, so the diverter fences
\* its record book: entries must run in non-decreasing ticket order.

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in 0..TicketLimit
  /\ obs \in [Sorters -> (0..TicketLimit) \cup {NoObs}]
  /\ ticket \in [Sorters -> 0..TicketLimit]
  /\ outstanding \in [Sorters -> [tk : 1..TicketLimit, bag : Bags] \cup {NoWrite}]
  /\ book \in Seq([tk : 1..TicketLimit, bag : Bags])

LastTicket == IF book = <<>> THEN 0 ELSE book[Len(book)].tk

BookFenced ==
  /\ \A i \in 1..Len(book) : book[i].tk <= reg
  /\ \A i \in 1..Len(book) : \A j \in 1..Len(book) : i < j => book[i].tk <= book[j].tk

Init ==
  /\ reg = 0
  /\ obs = [s \in Sorters |-> NoObs]
  /\ ticket = [s \in Sorters |-> 0]
  /\ outstanding = [s \in Sorters |-> NoWrite]
  /\ book = <<>>

ReadReg(s) ==
  /\ obs[s] = NoObs
  /\ obs' = [obs EXCEPT ![s] = reg]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, ticket, outstanding, book>>

Claim(s) ==
  /\ obs[s] = reg
  /\ reg < TicketLimit
  /\ reg' = reg + 1
  /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = reg + 1]
  /\ obs' = [obs EXCEPT ![s] = NoObs]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<outstanding, book>>

ClaimAbort(s) ==
  /\ obs[s] # NoObs
  /\ (obs[s] # reg \/ reg = TicketLimit)
  /\ obs' = [obs EXCEPT ![s] = NoObs]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, ticket, outstanding, book>>

Submit(s, b) ==
  /\ ticket[s] > 0
  /\ outstanding[s] = NoWrite
  /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![s] = [tk |-> ticket[s], bag |-> b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, obs, ticket, book>>

Honour(s) ==
  /\ outstanding[s] # NoWrite
  /\ Len(book) < BookSize
  /\ outstanding[s].tk >= LastTicket
  /\ book' = Append(book, outstanding[s])
  /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![s] = NoWrite]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, obs, ticket>>

Refuse(s) ==
  /\ outstanding[s] # NoWrite
  /\ (outstanding[s].tk < LastTicket \/ Len(book) = BookSize)
  /\ outstanding' = [outstanding EXCEPT ![s] = NoWrite]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, obs, ticket, book>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Sorters : ReadReg(s) \/ Claim(s) \/ ClaimAbort(s) \/ Honour(s) \/ Refuse(s)
  \/ \E s \in Sorters, b \in Bags : Submit(s, b)

InstructionSettled ==
  \A s \in Sorters : (outstanding[s] # NoWrite) ~> (outstanding[s] = NoWrite)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ SF_vars(Honour(SorterA)) /\ SF_vars(Refuse(SorterA)) /\ SF_vars(Honour(SorterB)) /\ SF_vars(Refuse(SorterB))
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  SorterA = sa
  SorterB = sb
  Bags = {bag1, bag2}
  NoObs = noobs
  NoWrite = nowrite
  TicketLimit = 2
  BookSize = 2
INVARIANT BookFenced
PROPERTY InstructionSettled
nl:
Terminal 3's baggage router has a single diverter that decides which chute each bag drops into. Several sorter controllers can drive the diverter, but only one of them at a time is supposed to be in charge. Which one is in charge is settled through a compare-and-swap on the router's ticket register. A controller that wants to take charge first reads the register, then attempts the swap by re-presenting the number it read; the swap only goes through if the register still holds that number, in which case the register is advanced by one and the controller keeps the new number as its ticket. If the register moved underneath it, or if the register has already reached the ticketing limit for the shift, the attempt is abandoned and the controller drops its reading.

Controllers in this terminal are slow, not broken. A controller that lost the register can still be alive and working from an old ticket -- it may have been paged out for a long while and then wake up and submit a diverter instruction it decided on ages ago. So the diverter itself does the policing. It keeps a written record of the instructions it has honoured, and it refuses any instruction whose ticket is older than the ticket on the last instruction it wrote down. An instruction from a slow controller with a superseded ticket is thrown away rather than acted on, and once the shift's record book is full every further instruction is thrown away too.

A controller holding any ticket at all may submit one diverter instruction at a time, naming a bag; it cannot submit another until the first one has been honoured or thrown away.

The property the terminal cares about is that the diverter's record book can never be read as if a stale controller had acted. The tickets written in the book must run in non-decreasing order from first entry to last, and no entry may carry a ticket that the register never issued.

The full action set is: ReadReg (a controller with no reading in hand samples the ticket register), Claim (a controller whose reading still matches the register, with the register below the shift limit, advances the register and takes the new value as its ticket, dropping its reading), ClaimAbort (a controller whose reading no longer matches, or which finds the register at the shift limit, drops its reading), Submit (a controller that owns a ticket and has no instruction outstanding submits an instruction for a bag, stamped with its ticket), Honour (the diverter appends an outstanding instruction to the record book, permitted only if its ticket is not older than the ticket on the last entry and the book is not full), Refuse (the diverter throws away an outstanding instruction whose ticket is older than the last entry's, or any outstanding instruction once the book is full).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The tickets recorded in the diverter's book are non-decreasing from the first entry to the last, and no recorded ticket is greater than the value the ticket register has reached.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No controller is left waiting on the diverter forever -- every instruction that has been submitted is eventually either honoured and written into the book or refused and thrown away, even when the submitting controller is a slow one.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m6p1t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Cranes, NoCrane, NoAmend, LeaseSpan, ShiftEnd, BookLimit

VARIABLES clock, holder, expiry, book, sending

vars == <<clock, holder, expiry, book, sending>>

\* The record book is the run of accepted amendments; its revision is Len(book).
\* Leases die by clock expiry, and the network reorders, so the book re-checks
\* the base revision at acceptance time. That check is what stops a lost update.

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in 0..ShiftEnd
  /\ holder \in Cranes \cup {NoCrane}
  /\ expiry \in 0..(ShiftEnd + LeaseSpan)
  /\ book \in Seq([by : Cranes, base : 0..BookLimit])
  /\ sending \in [Cranes -> [by : Cranes, base : 0..BookLimit] \cup {NoAmend}]

LiveLease(c) == holder = c /\ clock < expiry

NoLostAmendment == \A i \in 1..Len(book) : book[i].base = i - 1

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ holder = NoCrane
  /\ expiry = 0
  /\ book = <<>>
  /\ sending = [c \in Cranes |-> NoAmend]

GrantLease(c) ==
  /\ \A d \in Cranes : ~LiveLease(d)
  /\ holder' = c
  /\ expiry' = clock + LeaseSpan
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, book, sending>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < ShiftEnd
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, expiry, book, sending>>

Prepare(c) ==
  /\ LiveLease(c)
  /\ sending[c] = NoAmend
  /\ sending' = [sending EXCEPT ![c] = [by |-> c, base |-> Len(book)]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, expiry, book>>

Accept(c) ==
  /\ sending[c] # NoAmend
  /\ sending[c].base = Len(book)
  /\ LiveLease(sending[c].by)
  /\ Len(book) < BookLimit
  /\ book' = Append(book, sending[c])
  /\ sending' = [sending EXCEPT ![c] = NoAmend]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, expiry>>

Discard(c) ==
  /\ sending[c] # NoAmend
  /\ \/ sending[c].base # Len(book)
     \/ ~LiveLease(sending[c].by)
     \/ Len(book) = BookLimit
  /\ sending' = [sending EXCEPT ![c] = NoAmend]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, expiry, book>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : GrantLease(c) \/ Prepare(c) \/ Accept(c) \/ Discard(c)
  \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Cranes = {gantry1, gantry2}
  NoCrane = nocrane
  NoAmend = noamend
  LeaseSpan = 2
  ShiftEnd = 3
  BookLimit = 3
INVARIANT NoLostAmendment
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
The Vanheim container terminal keeps one shared stowage record for the vessel being worked. Gantry crane controllers amend that record every time a box is placed or shifted: each amendment says which crane made it and which revision of the record the crane was looking at when it decided on the change. The record itself is just the run of amendments accepted so far; its current revision number is simply how many amendments have been accepted.

Only a crane holding a valid yard lease may amend the record. A lease is granted to a crane when no crane currently holds a live one, and it is stamped with an expiry a fixed number of yard-clock ticks in the future. The yard clock advances on its own, and when it passes a lease's expiry that lease is simply dead -- there is no handshake, no revocation message, the holder just stops being the holder. That is the whole point of leasing rather than locking: a crane that has gone quiet does not wedge the record forever.

Amendments do not reach the record book instantly. A crane prepares an amendment against the revision it can see and hands it to the yard network, which delivers to the record book out of order and after arbitrary delay -- one crane's amendment can overtake another's. So the record book itself does the checking. It accepts an amendment only if the revision the amendment was computed against is still the current revision, and only if the crane that prepared it still holds a live, unexpired lease. Any amendment that fails either test is thrown away, and the crane must look at the record afresh and prepare a new one. A crane may only have one amendment in the network at a time.

What must never happen is a lost amendment: an amendment being accepted on top of a revision it never saw, so that the change it was overwriting silently disappears. Read against revision two, and you are only allowed to land on revision two.

The full action set is: GrantLease (a crane takes the yard lease when no live lease exists, stamped to expire a fixed number of ticks ahead), Tick (the yard clock advances by one, up to the end of the shift, possibly killing the live lease), Prepare (a crane holding a live lease and with nothing already in the network hands the network an amendment stamped with the revision it can currently see), Accept (the record book takes an amendment out of the network and appends it, but only if its stamped revision is still current, its preparer still holds a live lease, and the book is not yet at its shift limit), Discard (the record book throws away an amendment whose stamped revision is no longer current or whose preparer's lease has died).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every amendment in the record book was computed against exactly the revision that immediately precedes it, so the n-th accepted amendment always carries base revision n minus one and no amendment has ever been overwritten unseen.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m8p6t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS TeamA, TeamB, RoomA, RoomB, NoRoom, DeptLimit

VARIABLES cleared, permit, staffed, booked, handbacks

vars == <<cleared, permit, staffed, booked, handbacks>>

Teams == {TeamA, TeamB}
Rooms == {RoomA, RoomB}

\* Coarse department clearance must be taken before, and given up after, the
\* fine room permit. Theatres can be taken out of service at runtime, but only
\* while nothing is authorised against them, so no permit is ever left stale.

TypeOK ==
  /\ cleared \subseteq Teams
  /\ permit \in [Teams -> Rooms \cup {NoRoom}]
  /\ staffed \subseteq Rooms
  /\ booked \in [Rooms -> Teams \cup {NoRoom}]
  /\ handbacks \in 0..DeptLimit

PermitsAreLive ==
  \A t \in Teams : permit[t] # NoRoom => (t \in cleared /\ permit[t] \in staffed)

Init ==
  /\ cleared = {}
  /\ permit = [t \in Teams |-> NoRoom]
  /\ staffed = Rooms
  /\ booked = [r \in Rooms |-> NoRoom]
  /\ handbacks = 0

Clear(t) ==
  /\ t \notin cleared
  /\ Cardinality(cleared) < DeptLimit
  /\ cleared' = cleared \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<permit, staffed, booked, handbacks>>

Permit(t, r) ==
  /\ t \in cleared
  /\ permit[t] = NoRoom
  /\ r \in staffed
  /\ booked[r] = NoRoom
  /\ \A u \in Teams : permit[u] # r
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![t] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cleared, staffed, booked, handbacks>>

Book(t) ==
  /\ permit[t] # NoRoom
  /\ permit[t] \in staffed
  /\ booked[permit[t]] = NoRoom
  /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![permit[t]] = t]
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![t] = NoRoom]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cleared, staffed, handbacks>>

Release(r) ==
  /\ booked[r] # NoRoom
  /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![r] = NoRoom]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cleared, permit, staffed, handbacks>>

HandBack(t) ==
  /\ permit[t] # NoRoom
  /\ handbacks < DeptLimit
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![t] = NoRoom]
  /\ handbacks' = handbacks + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cleared, staffed, booked>>

Uncleared(t) ==
  /\ t \in cleared
  /\ permit[t] = NoRoom
  /\ cleared' = cleared \ {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<permit, staffed, booked, handbacks>>

Staff(r) ==
  /\ r \notin staffed
  /\ staffed' = staffed \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cleared, permit, booked, handbacks>>

Unstaff(r) ==
  /\ r \in staffed
  /\ booked[r] = NoRoom
  /\ \A t \in Teams : permit[t] # r
  /\ staffed' = staffed \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cleared, permit, booked, handbacks>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Teams : Clear(t) \/ Book(t) \/ HandBack(t) \/ Uncleared(t)
  \/ \E t \in Teams, r \in Rooms : Permit(t, r)
  \/ \E r \in Rooms : Release(r) \/ Staff(r) \/ Unstaff(r)

PermitSpent == \A t \in Teams : (permit[t] # NoRoom) ~> (permit[t] = NoRoom)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ SF_vars(Book(TeamA)) /\ SF_vars(Book(TeamB)) /\ SF_vars(Release(RoomA)) /\ SF_vars(Release(RoomB))
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  TeamA = teamA
  TeamB = teamB
  RoomA = orA
  RoomB = orB
  NoRoom = noroom
  DeptLimit = 2
INVARIANT PermitsAreLive
PROPERTY PermitSpent
nl:
Bellwater General books its operating rooms through a two-level authorisation scheme. Before a surgical team may touch the theatre schedule at all, it must be admitted at the department level: the duty coordinator issues a department clearance, and only a limited number of clearances exist at once. Holding a department clearance is not enough to book anything; the team must then be authorised at the room level, receiving a room permit that names one specific theatre. A room permit is only ever issued to a team that already holds a department clearance, for a theatre that is currently staffed, that is not already booked, and that no other team has been permitted for.

The staffed set of theatres changes during the day. Theatres are brought into service when staff are available and taken out of service when they are not; a theatre may only be taken out of service when nobody holds a permit for it and it is not currently booked, so the hospital never strands an authorisation on a theatre that has gone dark.

The nesting rule is what the whole scheme rests on. A team must give up its room permit before it gives up its department clearance -- a team may not drop out at the department level while still holding a room-level authorisation, because a permit held by a team the department no longer recognises is a stale authorisation, and a stale authorisation must never be honoured.

A team holding a room permit for a staffed, unbooked theatre uses it to book that theatre, which consumes the permit. A booked theatre is later released when the case finishes. A team may also simply hand its room permit back without booking.

The full action set is: Clear (the coordinator issues a department clearance to a team, while the number of outstanding clearances is under the department limit), Permit (a cleared team with no room permit receives a permit for a staffed, unbooked theatre that no other team is permitted for), Book (a team holding a permit for a staffed theatre books it, consuming the permit), Release (a booked theatre is freed when the case finishes), HandBack (a team returns its room permit unused), Uncleared (a team with no room permit gives up its department clearance), Staff (an unstaffed theatre is brought into service), Unstaff (a staffed theatre with no permit outstanding and no booking is taken out of service).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every team holding a room permit is a team the department still recognises as cleared, and the theatre named on that permit is still in service -- no room-level authorisation is ever held by a team that has dropped out at the department level or for a theatre that has gone dark.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A room permit is never held indefinitely -- every permit a team receives is eventually spent on a booking or handed back, so no theatre stays reserved by an idle permit forever.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m4p2t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS HallCalls, HardMax, StartDepth

VARIABLES waiting, inService, finished, accepted, depth

vars == <<waiting, inService, finished, accepted, depth>>

\* Backpressure lives in the Accept guard: a call is refused while the bounded
\* queue is at its current working depth, never dropped after admission.
\* The depth moves at runtime but may not shrink below what is already queued.

Queued == {waiting[i] : i \in 1..Len(waiting)}

TypeOK ==
  /\ waiting \in Seq(HallCalls)
  /\ inService \subseteq HallCalls
  /\ finished \subseteq HallCalls
  /\ accepted \subseteq HallCalls
  /\ depth \in 0..HardMax

CallsConserved ==
  /\ Queued \cup inService \cup finished = accepted
  /\ Queued \cap inService = {}
  /\ Queued \cap finished = {}
  /\ inService \cap finished = {}
  /\ \A i, j \in 1..Len(waiting) : i # j => waiting[i] # waiting[j]

Init ==
  /\ waiting = <<>>
  /\ inService = {}
  /\ finished = {}
  /\ accepted = {}
  /\ depth = StartDepth

Accept(c) ==
  /\ c \notin accepted
  /\ Len(waiting) < depth
  /\ waiting' = Append(waiting, c)
  /\ accepted' = accepted \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inService, finished, depth>>

Dispatch ==
  /\ Len(waiting) > 0
  /\ inService' = inService \cup {waiting[1]}
  /\ waiting' = Tail(waiting)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<finished, accepted, depth>>

Finish(c) ==
  /\ c \in inService
  /\ inService' = inService \ {c}
  /\ finished' = finished \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, accepted, depth>>

Shorten ==
  /\ depth > Len(waiting)
  /\ depth > 0
  /\ depth' = depth - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, inService, finished, accepted>>

Lengthen ==
  /\ depth < HardMax
  /\ depth' = depth + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, inService, finished, accepted>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in HallCalls : Accept(c) \/ Finish(c)
  \/ Dispatch
  \/ Shorten
  \/ Lengthen

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  HallCalls = {f2, f5, f9}
  HardMax = 3
  StartDepth = 2
INVARIANT CallsConserved
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
The Kestrel Tower elevator bank takes hall calls from the floors through a single bounded dispatch queue. A hall call that is accepted is written into the queue in arrival order; the queue has a working depth, and when the queue is already at that depth the dispatcher applies backpressure and simply does not accept the call -- the button stays lit and the passenger presses again later. Nothing is ever dropped on the floor: a call is refused up front or it is honoured, never silently swallowed once it is in.

The queue's working depth is not fixed. The bank's supervisor shortens the queue during maintenance windows, when diagnostics need the spare buffer, and lengthens it again afterwards up to the hardware maximum. Shortening is only permitted down to the number of calls currently waiting, so trimming the buffer never discards a call that is already in it.

The dispatcher takes calls off the front of the queue and puts them into service, where a car is on its way to the calling floor. A call in service is finished when the car arrives and the doors open, at which point the call is done and never comes back.

Because passengers press buttons repeatedly, the dispatcher will not accept a call for a floor it has already accepted; a call that is waiting, in service, or already finished is not accepted a second time.

The whole safety argument is one of conservation. Every hall call the dispatcher has ever accepted is at any moment in exactly one of three conditions: waiting in the queue, in service, or finished. It cannot be waiting twice over, it cannot be waiting and in service at once, and it cannot have evaporated from all three.

The full action set is: Accept (an unaccepted hall call is appended to the queue, provided the queue is shorter than its current working depth), Dispatch (the call at the front of the queue is removed from the queue and put into service), Finish (a call in service is completed and becomes finished), Shorten (the supervisor reduces the working depth by one, never below the number of calls currently in the queue), Lengthen (the supervisor increases the working depth by one, up to the hardware maximum).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every accepted hall call sits in exactly one of the queue, the in-service set, or the finished set -- those three are pairwise disjoint, no call appears twice within the queue, and together they account for exactly the calls that have been accepted.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m0p5t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS AgentA, AgentB, BatchOne, BatchTwo, NoNote, NoAgent, AmendLimit

VARIABLES rev, settled, note, wire

vars == <<rev, settled, note, wire>>

Agents == {AgentA, AgentB}
Batches == {BatchOne, BatchTwo}

\* Optimistic settlement: an agent notes a revision and the ledger only commits
\* while that note still matches. The winner bumps the revision past its own
\* ticket, which is what makes every surviving note demonstrably stale.

TypeOK ==
  /\ rev \in [Batches -> 0..(AmendLimit + 1)]
  /\ settled \in [Batches -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ note \in [Agents -> [Batches -> (0..(AmendLimit + 1)) \cup {NoNote}]]
  /\ wire \in [Batches -> Agents \cup {NoAgent}]

WiredOnce ==
  \A b \in Batches :
    /\ (wire[b] # NoAgent) <=> settled[b]
    /\ settled[b] => \A a \in Agents : note[a][b] # NoNote => note[a][b] < rev[b]

Init ==
  /\ rev = [b \in Batches |-> 0]
  /\ settled = [b \in Batches |-> FALSE]
  /\ note = [a \in Agents |-> [b \in Batches |-> NoNote]]
  /\ wire = [b \in Batches |-> NoAgent]

Prepare(a, b) ==
  /\ ~settled[b]
  /\ note[a][b] = NoNote
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![a][b] = rev[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, settled, wire>>

Commit(a, b) ==
  /\ ~settled[b]
  /\ note[a][b] = rev[b]
  /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![b] = rev[b] + 1]
  /\ settled' = [settled EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
  /\ wire' = [wire EXCEPT ![b] = a]
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![a][b] = NoNote]

Reject(a, b) ==
  /\ note[a][b] # NoNote
  /\ (settled[b] \/ note[a][b] # rev[b])
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![a][b] = NoNote]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, settled, wire>>

Amend(b) ==
  /\ ~settled[b]
  /\ rev[b] < AmendLimit
  /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![b] = rev[b] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<settled, note, wire>>

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Agents, b \in Batches : Prepare(a, b) \/ Commit(a, b) \/ Reject(a, b)
  \/ \E b \in Batches : Amend(b)

EveryBatchSettles == \A b \in Batches : <>settled[b]

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Prepare(AgentA, BatchOne)) /\ WF_vars(Commit(AgentA, BatchOne)) /\ WF_vars(Reject(AgentA, BatchOne)) /\ WF_vars(Prepare(AgentA, BatchTwo)) /\ WF_vars(Commit(AgentA, BatchTwo)) /\ WF_vars(Reject(AgentA, BatchTwo))
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  AgentA = agentA
  AgentB = agentB
  BatchOne = batch1
  BatchTwo = batch2
  NoNote = nonote
  NoAgent = noagent
  AmendLimit = 1
INVARIANT WiredOnce
PROPERTY EveryBatchSettles
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
Every evening the Clearing House settles a small number of interbank batches. Settling a batch is irreversible: the moment it settles, a wire instruction leaves the building with the name of the settlement agent who drove it, funds move at the central bank, and there is no unwinding it. A batch must therefore be wired at most once, and the wire record for a settled batch must forever name exactly the one agent whose attempt won.

Several settlement agents work the same batches at once, and they work optimistically rather than taking any kind of exclusive hold. An agent picks up a batch that is still open and notes the batch's current revision number. That noted revision is its ticket. Later, the agent presents its attempt to the ledger. The ledger compares the revision the agent noted with the batch's revision right now; only if they are still identical does the ledger settle the batch, bump the revision past the value the winner saw, and write the wire record. If the revisions differ -- or if the batch has already settled -- the attempt is refused, the agent's note is torn up, and the agent is free to pick the batch up again and try afresh.

The attempts do not arrive in the order they were made. An agent's attempt can sit in the queue while the clearing house amends the batch underneath it, and can be presented long after a competing agent has already been served. An amendment (a late correction to the batch's contents, permitted only while the batch is still open) also bumps the batch's revision, which is exactly what invalidates every note taken before it. Each agent keeps at most one outstanding note per batch.

Because the winning attempt bumps the revision past its own ticket, every attempt still outstanding for a settled batch is provably stale -- its noted revision is strictly below the batch's revision -- so no late-arriving duplicate can ever be mistaken for a fresh one and wire the same batch a second time.

The full action set is: Prepare (an agent with no outstanding note for an open batch notes that batch's current revision), Commit (the ledger settles an open batch for an agent whose noted revision still matches, bumping the revision and writing the wire record naming that agent), Reject (the ledger tears up an outstanding note whose revision no longer matches or whose batch has already settled), Amend (the clearing house corrects an open batch, bumping its revision up to the evening's amendment limit).

SAFETY PROPERTY: A batch carries a wire record exactly when it has settled, and once a batch has settled every note still outstanding against it has a strictly lower revision than the batch's current one, so no second wire can ever be issued for it.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every batch is eventually settled -- the optimistic retry loop cannot spin forever, because amendments run out and a fresh note eventually matches and commits.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m9p0t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Lobbies, Servers, NoLobby, EpochCap

VARIABLES epoch, alloc, held, lobbyEpoch, playing

vars == <<epoch, alloc, held, lobbyEpoch, playing>>

\* Two independent lobbies share one server pool; the epoch-stamped allocation
\* is the only thing arbitrating them. A hold recorded in a superseded epoch is
\* void, and no server may be held by both lobbies at once.

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..EpochCap
  /\ alloc \in [Servers -> Lobbies \cup {NoLobby}]
  /\ held \in [Lobbies -> SUBSET Servers]
  /\ lobbyEpoch \in [Lobbies -> 0..EpochCap]
  /\ playing \subseteq Servers

ExclusiveAndCurrent ==
  /\ \A x, y \in Lobbies : x # y => held[x] \cap held[y] = {}
  /\ \A l \in Lobbies : \A s \in held[l] : alloc[s] = l /\ lobbyEpoch[l] = epoch

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ alloc = [s \in Servers |-> NoLobby]
  /\ held = [l \in Lobbies |-> {}]
  /\ lobbyEpoch = [l \in Lobbies |-> 0]
  /\ playing = {}

Allocate(l, s) ==
  /\ alloc[s] = NoLobby
  /\ \A m \in Lobbies : s \notin held[m]
  /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![s] = l]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, held, lobbyEpoch, playing>>

Grab(l, s) ==
  /\ alloc[s] = l
  /\ lobbyEpoch[l] = epoch
  /\ \A m \in Lobbies : s \notin held[m]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![l] = held[l] \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alloc, lobbyEpoch, playing>>

Start(l, s) ==
  /\ s \in held[l]
  /\ s \notin playing
  /\ playing' = playing \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alloc, held, lobbyEpoch>>

Finish(s) ==
  /\ s \in playing
  /\ playing' = playing \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alloc, held, lobbyEpoch>>

Drop(l, s) ==
  /\ s \in held[l]
  /\ s \notin playing
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![l] = held[l] \ {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alloc, lobbyEpoch, playing>>

Resync(l) ==
  /\ lobbyEpoch[l] < epoch
  /\ held[l] = {}
  /\ lobbyEpoch' = [lobbyEpoch EXCEPT ![l] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alloc, held, playing>>

Rebalance ==
  /\ epoch < EpochCap
  /\ playing = {}
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ alloc' = [s \in Servers |-> NoLobby]
  /\ held' = [l \in Lobbies |-> {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyEpoch, playing>>

Next ==
  \/ \E l \in Lobbies, s \in Servers : Allocate(l, s) \/ Grab(l, s) \/ Start(l, s) \/ Drop(l, s)
  \/ \E s \in Servers : Finish(s)
  \/ \E l \in Lobbies : Resync(l)
  \/ Rebalance

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Lobbies = {frankfurt, saopaulo}
  Servers = {srv1, srv2}
  NoLobby = nolobby
  EpochCap = 2
INVARIANT ExclusiveAndCurrent
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
Skyrift's matchmaking runs out of two independent regional lobbies, one in Frankfurt and one in Sao Paulo. Neither lobby knows anything about the other's queues or timers, but they draw match hosts from one single shared pool of game servers. A game server is a critical resource: a server that is hosting a match must not have a second match started on it, so a lobby has to hold the server before it may start anything there.

Which lobby may hold which server is decided by the pool allocator, and the allocator's decisions are epoch-numbered. The allocator publishes an allocation -- a mapping from servers to lobbies -- and every allocation belongs to an epoch. A lobby may take hold of a server only if the current allocation gives that server to it, and when it takes hold it records the epoch it was working in. When the pool is rebalanced (a datacentre drains, a region's population spikes), the allocator bumps the epoch and clears the allocation. Any hold recorded in a superseded epoch is void: the lobby must let it go before it can be given anything new, and a lobby whose epoch record is behind cannot take hold of anything.

A lobby holding a server may start a match on it. A match ends and the server goes quiet again, but the lobby keeps its hold until it explicitly releases it. A lobby will not release a hold while a match is still running on that server. The allocator only rebalances once the pool has drained -- no match anywhere may be running -- and a rebalance revokes every outstanding hold along with the allocation, so a lobby that has not yet caught up to the new epoch simply cannot take hold of anything until it resyncs.

The property that matters is exclusion. The two lobbies are independent and never talk, so the only thing standing between them and two matches on one box is the allocator's epoch-stamped allocation. No server may ever be held by both lobbies at once, and any server a lobby holds must be one the current allocation assigns to it in the current epoch.

The full action set is: Allocate (the allocator assigns an unassigned, unheld server to a lobby in the current epoch), Grab (a lobby whose epoch record is current takes hold of a server the current allocation assigns to it), Start (a lobby starts a match on a server it holds and that is quiet), Finish (a running match ends and its server goes quiet), Drop (a lobby releases a hold on a server with no match running), Resync (a lobby holding nothing brings its epoch record up to the allocator's epoch), Rebalance (the allocator bumps the epoch, clears the whole allocation and revokes every outstanding hold, permitted only when no match is running anywhere in the pool).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No game server is ever held by both regional lobbies at the same time, and every held server is one the current allocation assigns to its holder in the epoch that holder is working in.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m1p5t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RingSize, Orders, NoMachine

VARIABLES token, workedBy, phase, record

vars == <<token, workedBy, phase, record>>

Machines == 1..RingSize
NextInRing(m) == IF m = RingSize THEN 1 ELSE m + 1

\* The right to settle circulates as a ring token; only the token holder may put
\* an order through the payment channel. Settling is irreversible, so a settled
\* order must never remain in any machine's hands as work in progress.

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Machines
  /\ workedBy \in [Orders -> Machines \cup {NoMachine}]
  /\ phase \in [Orders -> {"untouched", "inprogress", "settled"}]
  /\ record \in [Orders -> Machines \cup {NoMachine}]

SettledIsFinal ==
  \A o \in Orders :
    /\ (record[o] # NoMachine) <=> (phase[o] = "settled")
    /\ (phase[o] = "settled") => workedBy[o] = NoMachine

Init ==
  /\ token = 1
  /\ workedBy = [o \in Orders |-> NoMachine]
  /\ phase = [o \in Orders |-> "untouched"]
  /\ record = [o \in Orders |-> NoMachine]

TakeUp(m, o) ==
  /\ phase[o] = "untouched"
  /\ workedBy[o] = NoMachine
  /\ workedBy' = [workedBy EXCEPT ![o] = m]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "inprogress"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, record>>

Abandon(m, o) ==
  /\ phase[o] = "inprogress"
  /\ workedBy[o] = m
  /\ workedBy' = [workedBy EXCEPT ![o] = NoMachine]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "untouched"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, record>>

Settle(m, o) ==
  /\ token = m
  /\ phase[o] = "inprogress"
  /\ workedBy[o] = m
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "settled"]
  /\ workedBy' = [workedBy EXCEPT ![o] = NoMachine]
  /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![o] = m]
  /\ UNCHANGED token

PassToken ==
  /\ token' = NextInRing(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<workedBy, phase, record>>

SettleStep == \E m \in Machines, o \in Orders : Settle(m, o)

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines, o \in Orders : TakeUp(m, o) \/ Abandon(m, o) \/ Settle(m, o)
  \/ PassToken

InProgressResolves ==
  \A o \in Orders : (phase[o] = "inprogress") ~> (phase[o] # "inprogress")

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(PassToken) /\ SF_vars(SettleStep)
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  RingSize = 3
  Orders = {ord1, ord2}
  NoMachine = 0
INVARIANT SettledIsFinal
PROPERTY InProgressResolves
nl:
Trellick Vending runs a network of machines that share one payment settlement channel. Settling an order is irreversible: the customer's card is captured, the money is taken, and there is no second bite. An order must therefore be settled at most once, and once settled the record of which machine settled it must never be rewritten.

Because the machines share one channel, the right to settle circulates as a token around a ring. Exactly one machine holds the token at any moment, and the token is passed on to the next machine in the ring. A machine may only settle an order while it is actually holding the token. Machines in this fleet are slow rather than broken -- a machine can sit on the token for a long time while its modem wakes up, and it can leave an order it has taken up unsettled for a long while -- but the token always moves on eventually and no machine ever falls out of the ring.

An order starts life untouched. A machine takes an order up, which records that machine as the one working it; only the machine that took an order up may settle it, and only an untouched order may be taken up. A machine that decides not to go through with an order it took up abandons it, which returns the order to untouched and forgets the machine that had it. Settling an order marks it settled and writes the settling machine into the settlement record permanently; a settled order can never be taken up, abandoned or settled again.

The guarantee the fleet's accountants need is that the settlement record is consistent with the working state: no settled order is still sitting in some machine's hands as work in progress, and no order has a settlement record without being marked settled. If an already-settled order could still be held as in-progress work by a machine, that machine could put it through the channel a second time.

The full action set is: TakeUp (a machine takes up an untouched order, recording itself as the machine working it), Abandon (the machine working an order that has not been settled gives it back, returning the order to untouched), Settle (the machine holding the token settles an order it has taken up, marking it settled and writing itself into the settlement record), PassToken (the token moves from its holder to the next machine in the ring).

SAFETY PROPERTY: An order has a settlement record exactly when it is marked settled, and no order that is marked settled is still recorded as work in progress in any machine's hands.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No order stays in progress forever -- every order that a machine takes up is eventually settled or abandoned, because the token keeps circulating and reaches the machine holding it.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m8p2t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones, Sectors, PerSector, NoDrone

VARIABLES charge, claimed, imaging, surveyed, unclaimed

vars == <<charge, claimed, imaging, surveyed, unclaimed>>

Grid == Sectors \X (1..PerSector)

\* Coarse level: charge of a sector. Fine level: individual cells inside it.
\* Work never evaporates -- a cell handed back goes to the unclaimed pool -- and
\* no drone may be holding a cell outside the sector it has charge of.

TypeOK ==
  /\ charge \in [Sectors -> Drones \cup {NoDrone}]
  /\ claimed \in [Drones -> SUBSET Grid]
  /\ imaging \in [Drones -> SUBSET Grid]
  /\ surveyed \subseteq Grid
  /\ unclaimed \subseteq Grid

Holding(d) == claimed[d] \cup imaging[d]

GridConserved ==
  /\ unclaimed \cup surveyed \cup (UNION {Holding(d) : d \in Drones}) = Grid
  /\ unclaimed \cap surveyed = {}
  /\ \A d \in Drones :
       /\ Holding(d) \cap (unclaimed \cup surveyed) = {}
       /\ claimed[d] \cap imaging[d] = {}
       /\ \A c \in Holding(d) : charge[c[1]] = d
  /\ \A d, e \in Drones : d # e => Holding(d) \cap Holding(e) = {}

Init ==
  /\ charge = [s \in Sectors |-> NoDrone]
  /\ claimed = [d \in Drones |-> {}]
  /\ imaging = [d \in Drones |-> {}]
  /\ surveyed = {}
  /\ unclaimed = Grid

TakeSector(d, s) ==
  /\ charge[s] = NoDrone
  /\ charge' = [charge EXCEPT ![s] = d]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<claimed, imaging, surveyed, unclaimed>>

ClaimCell(d, c) ==
  /\ c \in unclaimed
  /\ charge[c[1]] = d
  /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![d] = claimed[d] \cup {c}]
  /\ unclaimed' = unclaimed \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<charge, imaging, surveyed>>

BeginImage(d, c) ==
  /\ c \in claimed[d]
  /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![d] = claimed[d] \ {c}]
  /\ imaging' = [imaging EXCEPT ![d] = imaging[d] \cup {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<charge, surveyed, unclaimed>>

FinishImage(d, c) ==
  /\ c \in imaging[d]
  /\ imaging' = [imaging EXCEPT ![d] = imaging[d] \ {c}]
  /\ surveyed' = surveyed \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<charge, claimed, unclaimed>>

HandBack(d, c) ==
  /\ c \in claimed[d]
  /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![d] = claimed[d] \ {c}]
  /\ unclaimed' = unclaimed \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<charge, imaging, surveyed>>

DropSector(d, s) ==
  /\ charge[s] = d
  /\ \A c \in Holding(d) : c[1] # s
  /\ charge' = [charge EXCEPT ![s] = NoDrone]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<claimed, imaging, surveyed, unclaimed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Drones, s \in Sectors : TakeSector(d, s) \/ DropSector(d, s)
  \/ \E d \in Drones, c \in Grid :
       ClaimCell(d, c) \/ BeginImage(d, c) \/ FinishImage(d, c) \/ HandBack(d, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Drones = {dr1, dr2}
  Sectors = {north, south}
  PerSector = 1
  NoDrone = nodrone
INVARIANT GridConserved
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
The Ridgeline wildfire surveillance swarm has to photograph a fixed grid of ground cells. The grid is carved into sectors, and each sector holds a fixed number of cells. Work is handed out in two levels. A drone first takes charge of a whole sector from the ground coordinator -- the coarse level -- and only then may it take individual cells inside that sector as its own work -- the fine level. A drone may never take a cell in a sector it does not have charge of, and it may not give up charge of a sector while it still has any work outstanding inside it.

Drones over a fire are slow, not lost. Radio windows are short, thermals throw them around, and a drone can sit on a claimed cell for a long time before it gets round to imaging it. The coordinator therefore never quietly takes work away from a slow drone and hands it to someone else. Work that comes back from a drone comes back to the unclaimed pool, explicitly, one cell at a time.

A cell begins unclaimed. A drone with charge of the cell's sector may claim it, at which point it is that drone's work. The drone begins imaging the cell, which is a distinct state: a cell being imaged is committed, and the drone will not hand it back mid-pass. When the pass completes the cell is surveyed and stays surveyed. A drone may hand back a cell it has claimed but not yet begun imaging, returning it to the unclaimed pool.

The accounting that matters to the incident commander is that the grid is conserved. Every cell in the grid is at any instant unclaimed, claimed by exactly one drone, being imaged by exactly one drone, or surveyed -- never two of those at once, never claimed by two drones, and never missing from all of them. Alongside that, every cell a drone is holding, claimed or mid-image, must lie in a sector that drone actually has charge of.

The full action set is: TakeSector (a drone takes charge of a sector nobody has charge of), ClaimCell (a drone with charge of a cell's sector moves that cell from the unclaimed pool into its own claimed work), BeginImage (a drone starts an imaging pass on a cell it has claimed, moving it from claimed to being imaged), FinishImage (an imaging pass completes and the cell becomes surveyed), HandBack (a drone returns a claimed, not-yet-imaging cell to the unclaimed pool), DropSector (a drone gives up charge of a sector in which it holds no claimed or imaging cells).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every grid cell is at all times in exactly one of unclaimed, claimed by one drone, being imaged by one drone, or surveyed, and every cell a drone holds lies in a sector that same drone has charge of.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m0p2t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS FobOne, FobTwo, Locks, NoTransit, VersionBudget

VARIABLES version, registry, transit, fitted

vars == <<version, registry, transit, fitted>>

Fobs == {FobOne, FobTwo}

\* Optimistic dispatch: a credential travels stamped with the registry version
\* it left under, and a stale stamp is refused rather than forced through.
\* Refusal hands the credential back, so the fixed fob population is conserved.

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in 0..VersionBudget
  /\ registry \subseteq Fobs
  /\ transit \in [Fobs -> [dest : Locks, stamp : 0..VersionBudget] \cup {NoTransit}]
  /\ fitted \in [Locks -> SUBSET Fobs]

InTransit == {f \in Fobs : transit[f] # NoTransit}
Installed == UNION {fitted[l] : l \in Locks}

FobsConserved ==
  /\ registry \cup InTransit \cup Installed = Fobs
  /\ registry \cap InTransit = {}
  /\ registry \cap Installed = {}
  /\ InTransit \cap Installed = {}
  /\ \A l, m \in Locks : l # m => fitted[l] \cap fitted[m] = {}

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ registry = Fobs
  /\ transit = [f \in Fobs |-> NoTransit]
  /\ fitted = [l \in Locks |-> {}]

Dispatch(f, l) ==
  /\ f \in registry
  /\ transit[f] = NoTransit
  /\ transit' = [transit EXCEPT ![f] = [dest |-> l, stamp |-> version]]
  /\ registry' = registry \ {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, fitted>>

Install(f) ==
  /\ transit[f] # NoTransit
  /\ transit[f].stamp = version
  /\ version < VersionBudget
  /\ fitted' = [fitted EXCEPT ![transit[f].dest] = fitted[transit[f].dest] \cup {f}]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ transit' = [transit EXCEPT ![f] = NoTransit]
  /\ UNCHANGED registry

Refuse(f) ==
  /\ transit[f] # NoTransit
  /\ (transit[f].stamp # version \/ version = VersionBudget)
  /\ registry' = registry \cup {f}
  /\ transit' = [transit EXCEPT ![f] = NoTransit]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, fitted>>

Revoke(f, l) ==
  /\ f \in fitted[l]
  /\ version < VersionBudget
  /\ fitted' = [fitted EXCEPT ![l] = fitted[l] \ {f}]
  /\ registry' = registry \cup {f}
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED transit

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Fobs, l \in Locks : Dispatch(f, l) \/ Revoke(f, l)
  \/ \E f \in Fobs : Install(f) \/ Refuse(f)

TransitSettles == \A f \in Fobs : (transit[f] # NoTransit) ~> (transit[f] = NoTransit)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ SF_vars(Install(FobOne)) /\ SF_vars(Refuse(FobOne)) /\ SF_vars(Install(FobTwo)) /\ SF_vars(Refuse(FobTwo))
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  FobOne = fob1
  FobTwo = fob2
  Locks = {frontdoor, backdoor}
  NoTransit = notransit
  VersionBudget = 2
INVARIANT FobsConserved
PROPERTY TransitSettles
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A Halden smart-home installation has a hub and several door locks. The household owns a fixed set of key credentials -- physical fobs, each with a serial number. A credential is at any moment either sitting in the hub's registry, in transit to a lock, or installed at exactly one lock. Credentials are not minted and not destroyed by the network: the fixed set is the fixed set, and the whole point of the transfer protocol is that a credential never gets duplicated onto two locks and never falls off the network entirely.

The hub does not hold a lock on the registry while a transfer is in flight; that would wedge the house every time a lock's radio went quiet. Instead it works optimistically. The registry carries a version number. When the hub dispatches a credential to a lock, the credential leaves the registry and travels stamped with the registry version as it was at dispatch. Home radio meshes deliver out of order and with long delays, so a dispatch can arrive at a lock after other traffic has already changed the registry underneath it.

The lock therefore checks the stamp on arrival. If the stamp still matches the registry version, the install goes through: the credential is installed at that lock and the registry version is bumped. If the stamp is stale -- or if the registry has already been bumped as many times as this provisioning session allows -- the install is refused and the credential is handed straight back into the hub's registry, where it can be dispatched again later. Nothing is dropped in either case.

A credential installed at a lock can be revoked by the householder, which returns it to the registry and bumps the registry version, invalidating any dispatch still in flight. Only one dispatch per credential may be in flight at a time.

The full action set is: Dispatch (the hub sends a credential that is sitting in the registry to a lock, stamping it with the current registry version and removing it from the registry), Install (a lock accepts an in-transit credential whose stamp matches the registry version, installing it and bumping the version, provided the session's version budget is not exhausted), Refuse (a lock rejects an in-transit credential whose stamp is stale, or any in-transit credential once the session's version budget is exhausted, returning it to the hub's registry), Revoke (the householder removes an installed credential from a lock, returning it to the registry and bumping the version).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every key credential the household owns is at all times either in the hub registry, in transit on exactly one dispatch, or installed at exactly one lock, and never in two of those conditions at once and never in none of them.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No credential is ever left in transit forever -- every dispatched credential eventually either completes its install at the lock or is handed back into the hub's registry.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m6p4t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS GateOne, GateTwo, Depth, LeaseBeats, PreOpenEnd, MaxGrant

VARIABLES beat, expiry, allowance, book, wire

vars == <<beat, expiry, allowance, book, wire>>

Gateways == {GateOne, GateTwo}

\* Leases promise slots of the opening-cross buffer and die by clock expiry.
\* Promised-but-unused slots stop being charged the instant a lease dies, so a
\* late submission from a dead lease must be rejected or the book would overrun.

Alive(g) == beat < expiry[g]
Promised(g) == IF Alive(g) THEN allowance[g] ELSE 0
StillPromised == Promised(GateOne) + Promised(GateTwo)

TypeOK ==
  /\ beat \in 0..PreOpenEnd
  /\ expiry \in [Gateways -> 0..(PreOpenEnd + LeaseBeats)]
  /\ allowance \in [Gateways -> 0..MaxGrant]
  /\ book \in 0..Depth
  /\ wire \in [Gateways -> BOOLEAN]

BufferNeverOverpromised == book + StillPromised <= Depth

Init ==
  /\ beat = 0
  /\ expiry = [g \in Gateways |-> 0]
  /\ allowance = [g \in Gateways |-> 0]
  /\ book = 0
  /\ wire = [g \in Gateways |-> FALSE]

Beat ==
  /\ beat < PreOpenEnd
  /\ beat' = beat + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<expiry, allowance, book, wire>>

GrantLease(g, n) ==
  /\ ~Alive(g)
  /\ n \in 1..MaxGrant
  /\ book + StillPromised + n <= Depth
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![g] = beat + LeaseBeats]
  /\ allowance' = [allowance EXCEPT ![g] = n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<beat, book, wire>>

SubmitOrder(g) ==
  /\ Alive(g)
  /\ allowance[g] > 0
  /\ ~wire[g]
  /\ wire' = [wire EXCEPT ![g] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<beat, expiry, allowance, book>>

AcceptOrder(g) ==
  /\ wire[g]
  /\ Alive(g)
  /\ allowance[g] > 0
  /\ book' = book + 1
  /\ allowance' = [allowance EXCEPT ![g] = allowance[g] - 1]
  /\ wire' = [wire EXCEPT ![g] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<beat, expiry>>

RejectOrder(g) ==
  /\ wire[g]
  /\ (~Alive(g) \/ allowance[g] = 0)
  /\ wire' = [wire EXCEPT ![g] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<beat, expiry, allowance, book>>

Next ==
  \/ Beat
  \/ \E g \in Gateways : SubmitOrder(g) \/ AcceptOrder(g) \/ RejectOrder(g)
  \/ \E g \in Gateways, n \in 1..MaxGrant : GrantLease(g, n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  GateOne = gwA
  GateTwo = gwB
  Depth = 3
  LeaseBeats = 2
  PreOpenEnd = 3
  MaxGrant = 2
INVARIANT BufferNeverOverpromised
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
In the ten minutes before the opening cross, the exchange builds the auction book. The book has a hard depth: the matching engine's opening-cross buffer holds a fixed number of orders and not one more. Order-entry gateways feed the book, and to stop them from collectively overrunning the buffer, each gateway must hold a lease before it may put anything in.

A lease is granted to a gateway for a stated allowance of book slots and expires a fixed number of clock beats later. The exchange clock beats forward on its own; leases are not revoked by message, they simply die when the clock passes their expiry. The exchange will only grant a lease whose allowance fits: the orders already in the book, plus every slot still promised by leases that are currently alive, plus the new allowance, must fit inside the buffer depth. A gateway may not hold two leases at once.

Order submissions do not arrive instantly and do not arrive in order. A gateway with an allowance left submits an order into the gateway network; the network delivers to the matching engine after an arbitrary delay, and submissions from different gateways can overtake each other. By the time a submission reaches the engine, the lease it was made under may well have expired -- and once a lease has expired its allowance is no longer being counted against the buffer, so honouring a late submission would let the book overrun the depth. The engine therefore checks: it accepts a submission only if the submitting gateway's lease is still alive and still has allowance left, in which case the order goes into the book and that gateway's remaining allowance drops by one. Otherwise the submission is rejected outright and the gateway must obtain a fresh lease. A gateway keeps at most one submission in the network at a time.

The exchange's obligation is that the buffer is never overrun -- and not just after the fact: the orders already in the book plus every slot still promised by live leases must always fit inside the depth, so the exchange can never have promised more of the buffer than it has.

The full action set is: Beat (the exchange clock advances by one, up to the end of the pre-open window, possibly killing live leases), GrantLease (a gateway with no live lease is granted an allowance that fits within what is left of the depth after the book and all live promises, expiring a fixed number of beats ahead), SubmitOrder (a gateway with a live lease, remaining allowance and nothing already in the network puts an order into the gateway network), AcceptOrder (the matching engine takes a submission out of the network and puts the order in the book, permitted only if the submitting gateway's lease is still alive with allowance remaining, decrementing that allowance), RejectOrder (the matching engine throws away a submission whose gateway's lease has died or has no allowance left).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of orders already in the auction book plus the total allowance still promised by leases that are currently alive never exceeds the opening-cross buffer depth.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m8p0t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS FirmOne, FirmTwo, Symbols, Nobody, NoSymbol

VARIABLES segLatch, bookLatch, stage, aim

vars == <<segLatch, bookLatch, stage, aim>>

Firms == {FirmOne, FirmTwo}

\* The coarse segment latch only serialises acquisition of the fine book latch
\* and is dropped before the work starts; the book latch is held all the way
\* through. Firms inside the critical section are exactly the book-latch holders.

TypeOK ==
  /\ segLatch \in Firms \cup {Nobody}
  /\ bookLatch \in [Symbols -> Firms \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ stage \in [Firms -> {"idle", "waiting", "hasseg", "hasbook", "amending"}]
  /\ aim \in [Firms -> Symbols \cup {NoSymbol}]

Inside(f) == stage[f] \in {"hasbook", "amending"}

CriticalIsExclusive ==
  /\ \A f, g \in Firms : (f # g /\ Inside(f) /\ Inside(g)) => aim[f] # aim[g]
  /\ \A f \in Firms : Inside(f) => (aim[f] # NoSymbol /\ bookLatch[aim[f]] = f)

Init ==
  /\ segLatch = Nobody
  /\ bookLatch = [s \in Symbols |-> Nobody]
  /\ stage = [f \in Firms |-> "idle"]
  /\ aim = [f \in Firms |-> NoSymbol]

Seek(f, s) ==
  /\ stage[f] = "idle"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![f] = "waiting"]
  /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![f] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<segLatch, bookLatch>>

TakeSegment(f) ==
  /\ stage[f] = "waiting"
  /\ segLatch = Nobody
  /\ segLatch' = f
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![f] = "hasseg"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLatch, aim>>

TakeBook(f) ==
  /\ stage[f] = "hasseg"
  /\ segLatch = f
  /\ bookLatch[aim[f]] = Nobody
  /\ bookLatch' = [bookLatch EXCEPT ![aim[f]] = f]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![f] = "hasbook"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<segLatch, aim>>

DropSegment(f) ==
  /\ stage[f] = "hasbook"
  /\ segLatch = f
  /\ segLatch' = Nobody
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![f] = "amending"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLatch, aim>>

Finish(f) ==
  /\ stage[f] = "amending"
  /\ bookLatch' = [bookLatch EXCEPT ![aim[f]] = Nobody]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![f] = "idle"]
  /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![f] = NoSymbol]
  /\ UNCHANGED segLatch

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Firms, s \in Symbols : Seek(f, s)
  \/ \E f \in Firms : TakeSegment(f) \/ TakeBook(f) \/ DropSegment(f) \/ Finish(f)

WaitingGetsIn == \A f \in Firms : (stage[f] = "waiting") ~> (stage[f] = "amending")

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ SF_vars(TakeSegment(FirmOne)) /\ SF_vars(TakeBook(FirmOne)) /\ SF_vars(DropSegment(FirmOne)) /\ SF_vars(Finish(FirmOne)) /\ SF_vars(TakeSegment(FirmTwo)) /\ SF_vars(TakeBook(FirmTwo)) /\ SF_vars(DropSegment(FirmTwo)) /\ SF_vars(Finish(FirmTwo))
=============================================================================
