SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  FirmOne = firmA
  FirmTwo = firmB
  Symbols = {sym1, sym2}
  Nobody = nobody
  NoSymbol = nosymbol
INVARIANT CriticalIsExclusive
PROPERTY WaitingGetsIn
nl:
Between the pre-open and the opening cross, member firms amend the books of the symbols they make markets in. Amending a symbol's book is a critical section: while a firm is amending a book, no other firm may be amending that same book, or the cross would be computed from a half-written state.

The exchange protects this with two levels of latch, taken in a fixed order. There is one coarse segment latch covering the whole trading segment, and one fine book latch for each symbol. A firm that wants to amend a symbol first states which symbol it is after. It then takes the segment latch, which only one firm can hold at a time. Holding the segment latch, it takes the book latch for its symbol -- it must not attempt the book latch without holding the segment latch, which is what stops two firms racing for the same book. Once it holds the book latch, it drops the segment latch immediately: the coarse latch is only there to serialise acquisition, not to serialise the actual work. It then amends its book, and finally drops the book latch and goes idle.

Because the coarse latch is dropped before the amendment begins, two firms working on different symbols amend at the same time, which is the whole point. Because the fine latch is held throughout the amendment, two firms never amend the same symbol at the same time.

Member firms here are slow, not failed. A firm can be in the middle of an amendment for a long stretch -- their risk checks are slow, their operators are on the phone -- but every firm does finish, drops its latches, and comes back. Nothing in the protocol lets a firm be forcibly stripped of a latch it holds; the only reason a firm ever waits is that the latch it needs is held by someone who is still working.

The full action set is: Seek (an idle firm names the symbol it intends to amend and starts waiting for the segment latch), TakeSegment (a waiting firm takes the free segment latch), TakeBook (a firm holding the segment latch takes the free book latch for the symbol it named), DropSegment (a firm that has got its book latch drops the segment latch and begins amending), Finish (an amending firm drops its book latch and goes idle).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two firms are ever inside the critical section for the same symbol at the same time, and any firm inside the critical section is the recorded holder of that symbol's book latch.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No firm waits forever -- a firm that has named its symbol and started waiting eventually reaches the amending stage, because latches are only ever held by firms that are still working and every working firm finishes.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m7p4t2 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS EngineOne, EngineTwo, Ceiling, MaxWant, NoFigure

VARIABLES drawn, figure, want, position

vars == <<drawn, figure, want, position>>

Engines == {EngineOne, EngineTwo}
Outstanding == position[EngineOne] + position[EngineTwo]

\* Two independent engines share one liquidity pool through a compare-and-swap
\* register. A lost update would leave the register understating real exposure,
\* and the next draw would then sail past the treasury ceiling.

TypeOK ==
  /\ drawn \in 0..Ceiling
  /\ figure \in [Engines -> (0..Ceiling) \cup {NoFigure}]
  /\ want \in [Engines -> 0..MaxWant]
  /\ position \in [Engines -> 0..Ceiling]

RegisterTrueAndCapped == drawn = Outstanding /\ drawn <= Ceiling

Init ==
  /\ drawn = 0
  /\ figure = [e \in Engines |-> NoFigure]
  /\ want = [e \in Engines |-> 0]
  /\ position = [e \in Engines |-> 0]

Observe(e) ==
  /\ figure[e] = NoFigure
  /\ figure' = [figure EXCEPT ![e] = drawn]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drawn, want, position>>

Intend(e, n) ==
  /\ figure[e] # NoFigure
  /\ want[e] = 0
  /\ n \in 1..MaxWant
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![e] = n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drawn, figure, position>>

Draw(e) ==
  /\ figure[e] # NoFigure
  /\ want[e] > 0
  /\ figure[e] = drawn
  /\ figure[e] + want[e] <= Ceiling
  /\ drawn' = figure[e] + want[e]
  /\ position' = [position EXCEPT ![e] = position[e] + want[e]]
  /\ figure' = [figure EXCEPT ![e] = NoFigure]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![e] = 0]

Abandon(e) ==
  /\ figure[e] # NoFigure
  /\ (figure[e] # drawn \/ figure[e] + want[e] > Ceiling)
  /\ figure' = [figure EXCEPT ![e] = NoFigure]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![e] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drawn, position>>

Repay(e, n) ==
  /\ n \in 1..MaxWant
  /\ position[e] >= n
  /\ drawn >= n
  /\ drawn' = drawn - n
  /\ position' = [position EXCEPT ![e] = position[e] - n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<figure, want>>

Next ==
  \/ \E e \in Engines : Observe(e) \/ Draw(e) \/ Abandon(e)
  \/ \E e \in Engines, n \in 1..MaxWant : Intend(e, n) \/ Repay(e, n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  EngineOne = engA
  EngineTwo = engB
  Ceiling = 3
  MaxWant = 2
  NoFigure = nofigure
INVARIANT RegisterTrueAndCapped
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
Meridian Bank runs its interbank settlement batches through two settlement engines that were commissioned years apart and share nothing except the bank's intraday liquidity pool. The pool has a hard credit ceiling set by treasury: the total drawn across both engines must never exceed it, because drawing past the ceiling would breach the bank's collateral posting at the central bank.

There is no coordinator between the two engines. What they share is a single drawn-amount register that says how much of the pool is currently drawn. The register is updated by compare-and-swap. An engine that wants liquidity first reads the register and remembers the figure it saw. It then decides how much it needs for the batch it is about to settle. When it attempts the draw, it re-presents the figure it read: the draw only goes through if the register still holds that figure, and if the figure it read plus what it wants is within the ceiling. On success the register is written with the sum the engine computed from its own reading, and the engine's own recorded position goes up by the same amount. If the register moved underneath it -- because the other engine drew or repaid in the meantime -- the attempt is thrown out and the engine has to read again and start over.

Repayment goes the other way and does not need the swap: an engine that has a recorded position repays part of it, and the register comes down by exactly that amount at the same instant the engine's position does.

The failure mode this is all built against is a lost update. If both engines read the same figure and both wrote back their own sum, one of the draws would vanish from the register while the money was still out, the register would understate what is actually drawn, and the next draw would sail past the ceiling on the strength of a figure that was never true. So two things have to hold together at all times: the register must be exactly the sum of what the two engines have recorded as drawn, and it must never exceed the ceiling.

The full action set is: Observe (an engine with no figure in hand reads the drawn register), Intend (an engine that has a figure in hand settles on the amount it wants to draw), Draw (an engine whose remembered figure still matches the register, and whose figure plus its intended amount fits inside the ceiling, writes the computed sum into the register and adds the amount to its own position, dropping its figure), Abandon (an engine whose remembered figure no longer matches the register, or whose intended amount would breach the ceiling, drops its figure and its intent), Repay (an engine with a recorded position pays some of it back, decreasing the register and its own position by the same amount at once).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared drawn register is at all times exactly the sum of the two engines' recorded positions, and never exceeds the treasury ceiling.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m9p4t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS BotOne, BotTwo, Zones, LimitMax, EpochCap, NoZone

VARIABLES epoch, limit, inside, permit, draining

vars == <<epoch, limit, inside, permit, draining>>

Bots == {BotOne, BotTwo}

\* Permits are promises of a slot and carry the epoch that promised them; a
\* reconfiguration revokes them all. The count that must fit under a zone limit
\* is occupancy plus outstanding promises, not occupancy alone.

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..EpochCap
  /\ limit \in [Zones -> 0..LimitMax]
  /\ inside \in [Bots -> Zones \cup {NoZone}]
  /\ permit \in [Bots -> (Zones \X (0..EpochCap)) \cup {NoZone}]
  /\ draining \subseteq Zones

Occupants(z) == {b \in Bots : inside[b] = z}
Promises(z) == {b \in Bots : permit[b] # NoZone /\ permit[b][1] = z /\ permit[b][2] = epoch}

NeverOverPromised ==
  \A z \in Zones : Cardinality(Occupants(z)) + Cardinality(Promises(z)) <= limit[z]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ limit = [z \in Zones |-> LimitMax]
  /\ inside = [b \in Bots |-> NoZone]
  /\ permit = [b \in Bots |-> NoZone]
  /\ draining = {}

IssuePermit(b, z) ==
  /\ permit[b] = NoZone
  /\ inside[b] = NoZone
  /\ z \notin draining
  /\ Cardinality(Occupants(z)) + Cardinality(Promises(z)) < limit[z]
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![b] = <<z, epoch>>]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, limit, inside, draining>>

Enter(b) ==
  /\ permit[b] # NoZone
  /\ permit[b][2] = epoch
  /\ permit[b][1] \notin draining
  /\ inside' = [inside EXCEPT ![b] = permit[b][1]]
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![b] = NoZone]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, limit, draining>>

Leave(b) ==
  /\ inside[b] # NoZone
  /\ inside' = [inside EXCEPT ![b] = NoZone]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, limit, permit, draining>>

Reconfigure(newLimit) ==
  /\ epoch < EpochCap
  /\ \A z \in Zones : newLimit[z] >= Cardinality(Occupants(z))
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ limit' = newLimit
  /\ permit' = [b \in Bots |-> NoZone]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inside, draining>>

StartDrain(z) ==
  /\ z \notin draining
  /\ draining' = draining \cup {z}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, limit, inside, permit>>

EndDrain(z) ==
  /\ z \in draining
  /\ Occupants(z) = {}
  /\ draining' = draining \ {z}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, limit, inside, permit>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bots, z \in Zones : IssuePermit(b, z)
  \/ \E b \in Bots : Enter(b) \/ Leave(b)
  \/ \E z \in Zones : StartDrain(z) \/ EndDrain(z)
  \/ \E nl \in [Zones -> 0..LimitMax] : Reconfigure(nl)

DrainCompletes == \A z \in Zones : (z \in draining) ~> (Occupants(z) = {})

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Leave(BotOne)) /\ WF_vars(Leave(BotTwo))
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  BotOne = bot1
  BotTwo = bot2
  Zones = {zoneA, zoneB}
  LimitMax = 2
  EpochCap = 1
  NoZone = nozone
INVARIANT NeverOverPromised
PROPERTY DrainCompletes
nl:
The Aldgate fulfilment centre runs a fleet of picking robots across several floor zones. Each zone has an occupancy limit -- aisle width, fire egress, and the charging bus all cap how many robots may be inside a zone at once -- and that limit is not a constant. The fleet controller republishes zone limits as the shift changes, and every republication is a reconfiguration that bumps the controller's epoch number.

A robot may not simply drive into a zone. It must first be issued an entry permit for that zone, and every permit is stamped with the epoch it was issued under. The controller only issues a permit if the zone still has room once you count both the robots already inside and the permits already issued for it and not yet used -- a permit is a promise of a slot, and the controller never promises more slots than the zone has. When the controller reconfigures, every outstanding permit is revoked in the same breath, because those permits were promises against limits that no longer apply; a robot then has to ask again under the new epoch. A robot with a current permit drives into the zone, consuming the permit. A robot inside a zone drives out of it when its pick is done.

The floor supervisor has a privileged override: she can put a zone into drain. While a zone is draining no permit is issued for it and no robot enters it, so the robots inside can only leave. Once the zone is empty she takes it out of drain and normal working resumes. She uses this to get an engineer onto the floor safely.

Reconfiguration may also change the limits themselves, but the controller will not set a zone's limit below the number of robots already standing in it -- you cannot make a robot vanish by editing a number.

The full action set is: IssuePermit (the controller issues an epoch-stamped entry permit for a zone to a permit-less robot, only while the zone is not draining and the robots inside plus the permits outstanding for it are strictly under the zone's limit), Enter (a robot holding a current-epoch permit for a zone that is not draining and still under its limit drives in, consuming the permit), Leave (a robot inside a zone drives out), Reconfigure (the controller bumps its epoch, republishes each zone's limit at any value not below that zone's current occupancy, and revokes every outstanding permit), StartDrain (the supervisor puts a zone into drain), EndDrain (the supervisor takes an empty zone out of drain).

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every zone, the number of robots inside it plus the number of unused current-epoch permits outstanding for it never exceeds that zone's published limit.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A drain always completes -- once the supervisor puts a zone into drain, that zone eventually becomes empty of robots.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m8p4t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Flights, Runways, WindowCap, NoRunway

VARIABLES flow, slot, rolling, airborne

vars == <<flow, slot, rolling, airborne>>

\* Coarse flow release must precede a fine runway slot, and a held slot counts
\* against the window capacity just as a rolling aircraft does, because the slot
\* is a movement the tower has already committed to.

TypeOK ==
  /\ flow \subseteq Flights
  /\ slot \in [Flights -> Runways \cup {NoRunway}]
  /\ rolling \subseteq Flights
  /\ airborne \subseteq Flights

Holders == {f \in Flights : slot[f] # NoRunway}
Committed == Cardinality(Holders) + Cardinality(rolling)

MovementsWithinWindow ==
  /\ Committed <= WindowCap
  /\ \A f \in Holders \cup rolling : f \in flow

Init ==
  /\ flow = {}
  /\ slot = [f \in Flights |-> NoRunway]
  /\ rolling = {}
  /\ airborne = {}

FlowRelease(f) ==
  /\ f \notin flow
  /\ f \notin airborne
  /\ flow' = flow \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slot, rolling, airborne>>

GrantSlot(f, r) ==
  /\ f \in flow
  /\ slot[f] = NoRunway
  /\ f \notin rolling
  /\ f \notin airborne
  /\ \A g \in Flights : slot[g] # r
  /\ Committed < WindowCap
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![f] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<flow, rolling, airborne>>

LineUp(f) ==
  /\ slot[f] # NoRunway
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![f] = NoRunway]
  /\ rolling' = rolling \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<flow, airborne>>

Depart(f) ==
  /\ f \in rolling
  /\ rolling' = rolling \ {f}
  /\ airborne' = airborne \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<flow, slot>>

GiveUpSlot(f) ==
  /\ slot[f] # NoRunway
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![f] = NoRunway]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<flow, rolling, airborne>>

FlowWithdraw(f) ==
  /\ f \in flow
  /\ slot[f] = NoRunway
  /\ f \notin rolling
  /\ flow' = flow \ {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slot, rolling, airborne>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Flights, r \in Runways : GrantSlot(f, r)
  \/ \E f \in Flights :
       FlowRelease(f) \/ LineUp(f) \/ Depart(f) \/ GiveUpSlot(f) \/ FlowWithdraw(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Flights = {fl1, fl2, fl3}
  Runways = {rw27, rw33}
  WindowCap = 2
  NoRunway = norunway
INVARIANT MovementsWithinWindow
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
Approach control at a two-runway airport hands out departure movements in two stages. The coarse stage is the flow release: a flight is put on the departure flow list by the flow manager, which is what makes it eligible to be considered at all. The fine stage is the runway slot: a flight that is already on the flow list is given a specific runway slot, and a runway slot is only ever given to one flight at a time. A flight cannot be given a runway slot without being on the flow list first, and the flow manager will not take a flight off the flow list while it still holds a slot or is on the runway.

The runway complex has a movement capacity for the working window: the number of departures the tower is committed to at any instant. What counts against that capacity is not just the aircraft physically rolling -- a flight sitting on a slot is already a committed movement, because the slot is being held open for it. So the tower counts held slots and rolling aircraft together, and it will not issue another slot unless that combined figure is strictly under the window capacity. Handing a slot over to the roll is capacity-neutral: the slot is given up at the same instant the aircraft starts rolling.

Crews here are slow, not missing. A flight can sit on its slot for a long time -- a late passenger, a de-icing queue, a slow load sheet -- and the tower does not snatch the slot back to give it to somebody quicker. The only ways a slot stops being held are that the flight starts its roll, or the crew gives the slot up themselves.

The full action set is: FlowRelease (the flow manager puts a flight on the departure flow list), GrantSlot (a flight on the flow list, not already on a slot and not rolling or airborne, is given a free runway slot, provided the held slots plus the rolling aircraft are strictly under the window capacity), LineUp (a flight holding a slot gives the slot up and begins its roll), Depart (a rolling flight gets airborne and stops occupying the runway complex), GiveUpSlot (a crew hands its slot back without rolling), FlowWithdraw (the flow manager takes a flight with no slot and no roll off the flow list).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of flights holding a runway slot plus the number of flights rolling never exceeds the runway complex's window capacity, and every flight in either of those conditions is a flight that is on the departure flow list.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m7p1t0 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Steady, Fragile, NoMark, Budget

VARIABLES version, mark, used, dead

vars == <<version, mark, used, dead>>

Machines == {Steady, Fragile}

\* Compare-and-swap rather than a lock, because the fragile machine can stop
\* dead without telling anyone. The consumed-version set must stay exactly the
\* run below the current version: a lost update would leave a hole in it.

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in 0..Budget
  /\ mark \in [Machines -> (0..Budget) \cup {NoMark}]
  /\ used \subseteq 0..Budget
  /\ dead \in BOOLEAN

EveryVersionAttributed == used = {v \in 0..Budget : v < version}

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ mark = [m \in Machines |-> NoMark]
  /\ used = {}
  /\ dead = FALSE

Alive(m) == m = Steady \/ ~dead

Read(m) ==
  /\ Alive(m)
  /\ mark[m] = NoMark
  /\ mark' = [mark EXCEPT ![m] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, used, dead>>

Apply(m) ==
  /\ Alive(m)
  /\ mark[m] = version
  /\ version < Budget
  /\ used' = used \cup {version}
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ mark' = [mark EXCEPT ![m] = NoMark]
  /\ UNCHANGED dead

Discard(m) ==
  /\ Alive(m)
  /\ mark[m] # NoMark
  /\ (mark[m] # version \/ version = Budget)
  /\ mark' = [mark EXCEPT ![m] = NoMark]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, used, dead>>

Crash ==
  /\ ~dead
  /\ dead' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, mark, used>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Read(m) \/ Apply(m) \/ Discard(m)
  \/ Crash

RecordAdvances == <>(version = Budget)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ SF_vars(Read(Steady)) /\ SF_vars(Apply(Steady)) /\ SF_vars(Discard(Steady))
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Steady = steady
  Fragile = fragile
  NoMark = nomark
  Budget = 3
INVARIANT EveryVersionAttributed
PROPERTY RecordAdvances
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
Trellick Vending's machines all read and write one shared stock record for the product line they carry. The record is versioned: every accepted change moves it from one version to the next, and the version number is the record's history in miniature. What the operator cannot tolerate is a lost update -- two machines both writing a change computed from version four, both being accepted, and the record ending at version six with only one of the two changes actually reflected in it. Every version transition must be attributable to exactly one accepted change, with no gaps and no version consumed twice.

The machines coordinate without any lock, because one machine in the fleet can crash silently: its modem dies mid-shift and it simply stops, with no notification to anyone. A lock held by that machine would freeze the record for the rest of the fleet. So the record is updated by compare-and-swap instead. A machine reads the record's version and keeps the number it saw. When it presents its change it re-presents that number; the record only accepts the change if it is still at that version, in which case the version it consumed is marked used and the record moves on by one. If another machine got there first, the number no longer matches, the change is thrown out, and the machine reads again and recomputes.

One of the two machines in this network is the reliable one, wired to mains power and a fixed line. The other is the one that may crash silently at any moment; a crashed machine never acts again -- it does not read, it does not present, it does not recover. The reliable machine keeps working regardless, and the record keeps advancing to the end of the shift's version budget whether or not the other machine is alive, which is exactly the property that a lock would have destroyed.

The full action set is: Read (a machine that is not crashed and has no version number in hand reads the record's current version), Apply (a machine whose remembered version still matches the record's, with the shift's version budget not yet exhausted, has its change accepted -- the version it consumed is marked used and the record advances by one -- and drops its number), Discard (a machine whose remembered version no longer matches, or which finds the version budget exhausted, drops its number and must read afresh), Crash (the unreliable machine dies silently and takes no further action of any kind).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of versions that have been consumed by an accepted change is exactly the set of versions below the record's current version -- every version transition is accounted for by exactly one accepted change, so no change has ever been overwritten by another.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The shared record eventually reaches the end of the shift's version budget, even if the unreliable machine crashes silently at the worst possible moment.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m6p2t3 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, Totes, NoTote, LeaseTicks, ShiftEnd

VARIABLES clock, leaseEnd, grip, shelf, stranded, chute

vars == <<clock, leaseEnd, grip, shelf, stranded, chute>>

\* Leases die by clock, not by handshake, so a quiet robot can still be holding
\* a tote when its lease ends. Stranding moves that tote out of its grippers
\* rather than pretending it is back on the shelf: nothing is lost or doubled.

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in 0..ShiftEnd
  /\ leaseEnd \in [Robots -> 0..(ShiftEnd + LeaseTicks)]
  /\ grip \in [Robots -> Totes \cup {NoTote}]
  /\ shelf \subseteq Totes
  /\ stranded \subseteq Totes
  /\ chute \subseteq Totes

Live(r) == clock < leaseEnd[r]
Gripped == {t \in Totes : \E r \in Robots : grip[r] = t}

TotesConserved ==
  /\ shelf \cup stranded \cup chute \cup Gripped = Totes
  /\ shelf \cap stranded = {} /\ shelf \cap chute = {} /\ stranded \cap chute = {}
  /\ Gripped \cap (shelf \cup stranded \cup chute) = {}
  /\ \A r, q \in Robots : (r # q /\ grip[r] # NoTote) => grip[r] # grip[q]

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ leaseEnd = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
  /\ grip = [r \in Robots |-> NoTote]
  /\ shelf = Totes
  /\ stranded = {}
  /\ chute = {}

GrantLease(r) ==
  /\ \A q \in Robots : ~Live(q)
  /\ leaseEnd' = [leaseEnd EXCEPT ![r] = clock + LeaseTicks]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, grip, shelf, stranded, chute>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < ShiftEnd
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseEnd, grip, shelf, stranded, chute>>

Pickup(r, t) ==
  /\ Live(r)
  /\ grip[r] = NoTote
  /\ t \in shelf
  /\ grip' = [grip EXCEPT ![r] = t]
  /\ shelf' = shelf \ {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, leaseEnd, stranded, chute>>

Deposit(r) ==
  /\ Live(r)
  /\ grip[r] # NoTote
  /\ chute' = chute \cup {grip[r]}
  /\ grip' = [grip EXCEPT ![r] = NoTote]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, leaseEnd, shelf, stranded>>

Strand(r) ==
  /\ ~Live(r)
  /\ grip[r] # NoTote
  /\ stranded' = stranded \cup {grip[r]}
  /\ grip' = [grip EXCEPT ![r] = NoTote]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, leaseEnd, shelf, chute>>

Recover(t) ==
  /\ t \in stranded
  /\ stranded' = stranded \ {t}
  /\ shelf' = shelf \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, leaseEnd, grip, chute>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Robots : GrantLease(r) \/ Deposit(r) \/ Strand(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, t \in Totes : Pickup(r, t)
  \/ \E t \in Totes : Recover(t)
  \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Robots = {rbt1, rbt2}
  Totes = {tote1, tote2}
  NoTote = notote
  LeaseTicks = 2
  ShiftEnd = 3
INVARIANT TotesConserved
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
The Aldgate robot fleet moves totes from the shelves to the outbound chute. A tote is a physical object and the warehouse's inventory count depends on never inventing one and never losing one: at any instant every tote is on a shelf, in the grippers of exactly one robot, on the stranded list, or already in the outbound chute.

A robot may not pick a tote up unless it holds a live carry lease. Leases are granted by the fleet controller, are stamped to expire a fixed number of ticks of the warehouse clock in the future, and are never revoked by message -- the clock simply passes the expiry and the lease is dead. Only one robot holds a live lease at a time. The controller uses leases rather than a handshake precisely because robots here are slow, not lost: a robot can go quiet for a long stretch in a dead radio spot, and the fleet must be able to carry on without waiting for it to answer.

That, though, creates the awkward case the stranded list exists for. A robot can still be physically holding a tote when its lease dies. The controller does not pretend the tote is back on the shelf, and it does not let another robot pick up the same tote: the tote is moved onto the stranded list, out of the quiet robot's grippers and out of circulation, and it stays there until a floor walker recovers it and puts it back on a shelf. A robot with a live lease that is carrying a tote can instead deposit it in the outbound chute, where it stays for good.

The full action set is: GrantLease (the controller grants the carry lease to a robot when no live lease exists, stamped to expire a fixed number of ticks ahead), Tick (the warehouse clock advances by one, up to the end of the shift, possibly killing the live lease), Pickup (a robot with a live lease and empty grippers takes a tote off a shelf), Deposit (a robot with a live lease puts the tote it is carrying into the outbound chute), Strand (a tote carried by a robot whose lease has died is moved onto the stranded list and out of that robot's grippers), Recover (a floor walker takes a tote off the stranded list and puts it back on a shelf).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every tote is at all times in exactly one of: on a shelf, carried by exactly one robot, on the stranded list, or in the outbound chute -- never in two of those at once, never carried by two robots, and never absent from all of them.

EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS BotOne, BotTwo, PalletOne, PalletTwo, NoOrder, PlanLimit

VARIABLES epoch, order, orderEp, manifest, sealed

vars == <<epoch, order, orderEp, manifest, sealed>>

Bots == {BotOne, BotTwo}
Pallets == {PalletOne, PalletTwo}

\* Seal orders carry the plan epoch that produced them; a republication makes
\* every outstanding order stale. Sealing is irreversible, so the manifest must
\* never list a pallet twice and must agree exactly with what is sealed.

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..PlanLimit
  /\ order \in [Bots -> Pallets \cup {NoOrder}]
  /\ orderEp \in [Bots -> 0..PlanLimit]
  /\ manifest \in Seq(Pallets)
  /\ sealed \subseteq Pallets

Listed == {manifest[i] : i \in 1..Len(manifest)}

ManifestIsFaithful ==
  /\ \A i, j \in 1..Len(manifest) : i # j => manifest[i] # manifest[j]
  /\ Listed = sealed

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ order = [b \in Bots |-> NoOrder]
  /\ orderEp = [b \in Bots |-> 0]
  /\ manifest = <<>>
  /\ sealed = {}

Assign(b, p) ==
  /\ order[b] = NoOrder
  /\ p \notin sealed
  /\ \A c \in Bots : order[c] # p
  /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![b] = p]
  /\ orderEp' = [orderEp EXCEPT ![b] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, manifest, sealed>>

Seal(b) ==
  /\ order[b] # NoOrder
  /\ orderEp[b] = epoch
  /\ order[b] \notin sealed
  /\ manifest' = Append(manifest, order[b])
  /\ sealed' = sealed \cup {order[b]}
  /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![b] = NoOrder]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, orderEp>>

DropStale(b) ==
  /\ order[b] # NoOrder
  /\ orderEp[b] < epoch
  /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![b] = NoOrder]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, orderEp, manifest, sealed>>

Republish ==
  /\ epoch < PlanLimit
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<order, orderEp, manifest, sealed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bots, p \in Pallets : Assign(b, p)
  \/ \E b \in Bots : Seal(b) \/ DropStale(b)

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  BotOne = bot1
  BotTwo = bot2
  PalletOne = pal1
  PalletTwo = pal2
  NoOrder = noorder
  PlanLimit = 2
INVARIANT ManifestIsFaithful
PROPERTY AllPalletsSealed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
At the end of the Aldgate pick line, robots seal pallets for dispatch. Sealing is irreversible: the shrink wrap goes on, the dispatch label is printed and burned into the outbound manifest, and the pallet leaves the building. A pallet that got sealed twice would be shipped twice, so the manifest must never carry the same pallet in two places, and the manifest is the authoritative record of exactly which pallets have been sealed.

Which robot seals which pallet is set by the dispatch plan, and the plan is epoch-numbered. Every seal order handed to a robot is stamped with the epoch of the plan it came from. When the line supervisor republishes the plan -- a lane closes, a carrier's cut-off moves, a customer consolidates two orders -- the epoch goes up by one, and every order stamped with an older epoch is stale. A robot may only seal under an order whose stamp is the current epoch; a robot carrying a stale order drops it and waits to be given a new one.

Robots on this line are slow, not failed. A robot can be given an order and then take a very long time to act on it -- it is finishing another aisle, it is charging, its wrap head is warming up. Nothing takes an order away from a slow robot except a republication of the plan, and a pallet that is already under someone's order is not handed to a second robot. Every robot does eventually act.

Only unsealed pallets are ever assigned, and a robot holds at most one seal order at a time.

The full action set is: Assign (a robot with no order is given a seal order for an unsealed pallet that no other robot is holding an order for, stamped with the current plan epoch), Seal (a robot whose order carries the current epoch seals its pallet, which appends the pallet to the outbound manifest, marks it sealed, and clears the robot's order), DropStale (a robot whose order carries a superseded epoch discards it), Republish (the supervisor bumps the plan epoch, up to the day's limit, which makes every outstanding order stale).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No pallet appears more than once in the outbound manifest, and the pallets listed in the manifest are exactly the pallets recorded as sealed.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every pallet is eventually sealed -- republications and slow robots can delay a seal but cannot prevent it, because the plan stops changing and every order is eventually acted on or replaced.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m7p0t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, Clear, NoPeek, MaxForced

VARIABLES reg, peek, inSection, armed, forced

vars == <<reg, peek, inSection, armed, forced>>

\* Entry to the single line is bid for by compare-and-swap on the occupancy
\* register. The signaller's override may only clear the register with the
\* section confirmed empty -- otherwise a second train could swap in behind.

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in Trains \cup {Clear}
  /\ peek \in [Trains -> Trains \cup {Clear, NoPeek}]
  /\ inSection \subseteq Trains
  /\ armed \in BOOLEAN
  /\ forced \in 0..MaxForced

SectionExclusive ==
  /\ \A t, u \in Trains : (t # u) => ~(t \in inSection /\ u \in inSection)
  /\ \A t \in inSection : reg = t

Init ==
  /\ reg = Clear
  /\ peek = [t \in Trains |-> NoPeek]
  /\ inSection = {}
  /\ armed = FALSE
  /\ forced = 0

Peek(t) ==
  /\ peek[t] = NoPeek
  /\ peek' = [peek EXCEPT ![t] = reg]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, inSection, armed, forced>>

Swap(t) ==
  /\ peek[t] = Clear
  /\ reg = Clear
  /\ reg' = t
  /\ peek' = [peek EXCEPT ![t] = NoPeek]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inSection, armed, forced>>

SwapFail(t) ==
  /\ peek[t] # NoPeek
  /\ (peek[t] # reg \/ reg # Clear)
  /\ peek' = [peek EXCEPT ![t] = NoPeek]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, inSection, armed, forced>>

Enter(t) ==
  /\ reg = t
  /\ inSection = {}
  /\ inSection' = {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, peek, armed, forced>>

Exit(t) ==
  /\ t \in inSection
  /\ inSection' = inSection \ {t}
  /\ reg' = Clear
  /\ UNCHANGED <<peek, armed, forced>>

Arm ==
  /\ ~armed
  /\ forced < MaxForced
  /\ armed' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, peek, inSection, forced>>

ForceClear ==
  /\ armed
  /\ inSection = {}
  /\ reg # Clear
  /\ reg' = Clear
  /\ armed' = FALSE
  /\ forced' = forced + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<peek, inSection>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains : Peek(t) \/ Swap(t) \/ SwapFail(t) \/ Enter(t) \/ Exit(t)
  \/ Arm
  \/ ForceClear

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Trains = {up1, dn2}
  Clear = clear
  NoPeek = nopeek
  MaxForced = 2
INVARIANT SectionExclusive
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
On the branch beyond Ferrier Junction there is a single-track section that both up and down trains must use. It is a critical resource in the strictest sense: two trains inside it at once is a head-on collision, so at most one train may ever be inside.

There is no signalbox on the branch any more. Entry is arbitrated by a solid-state occupancy register at the junction, and trains bid for it with a compare-and-swap. A train first peeks at the register, remembering what it saw. It then attempts the swap, re-presenting what it read: the swap only succeeds if the register still reads exactly that and what it read was "clear", in which case the register is written with that train's own identity. If the register moved in between -- another train got there first, or the signaller intervened -- the attempt fails and the train drops what it peeked and may peek again.

A train may only pass the entry board and go into the section once the register carries its own identity, and only when the section is physically empty. When it comes out the far end it writes the register back to clear in the same movement as it leaves the section.

There is one privileged override. The area signaller can arm a release and then force the register back to clear -- for a train that has failed in section and been dragged out by a rescue loco, or for a register left showing an identity after a comms fault. The override is deliberately hobbled: the signaller may only force the register clear when the section is confirmed physically empty. That confirmation is the entire safety case for the override, because forcing a register clear with a train still inside would let a second train swap itself in and follow it onto the single line.

The full action set is: Peek (a train with nothing remembered reads the occupancy register), Swap (a train whose remembered reading still matches the register and read it as clear writes its own identity into the register and drops the reading), SwapFail (a train whose remembered reading no longer matches the register, or which read something other than clear, drops the reading), Enter (a train whose identity is in the register moves into the empty section), Exit (a train in the section leaves it and writes the register back to clear in the same movement), Arm (the signaller arms the release), ForceClear (the armed signaller writes the register back to clear, permitted only when no train is inside the section, and disarms).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two trains are ever inside the single-track section at the same time, and any train inside the section is the train whose identity the occupancy register currently carries.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m6p3t5 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS GuestOne, GuestTwo, Slots, NoSlot, NoGuest, LeaseHours, DayEnd

VARIABLES clock, allocOf, tableOf, dueAt, pinned

vars == <<clock, allocOf, tableOf, dueAt, pinned>>

Guests == {GuestOne, GuestTwo}

\* Guest slots are leased, not granted: they come back when the hub clock passes
\* the expiry, or at the day boundary. The table and the guests' allocations must
\* mirror each other, which is what rules out one slot serving two guests.

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in 0..DayEnd
  /\ allocOf \in [Guests -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ tableOf \in [Slots -> Guests \cup {NoGuest}]
  /\ dueAt \in [Guests -> 0..(DayEnd + LeaseHours)]
  /\ pinned \subseteq Slots

TableMirrorsAllocations ==
  /\ \A g \in Guests : allocOf[g] # NoSlot => tableOf[allocOf[g]] = g
  /\ \A s \in Slots : tableOf[s] # NoGuest => allocOf[tableOf[s]] = s
  /\ \A s \in pinned : tableOf[s] = NoGuest

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ allocOf = [g \in Guests |-> NoSlot]
  /\ tableOf = [s \in Slots |-> NoGuest]
  /\ dueAt = [g \in Guests |-> 0]
  /\ pinned = {}

Allocate(g, s) ==
  /\ allocOf[g] = NoSlot
  /\ tableOf[s] = NoGuest
  /\ s \notin pinned
  /\ allocOf' = [allocOf EXCEPT ![g] = s]
  /\ tableOf' = [tableOf EXCEPT ![s] = g]
  /\ dueAt' = [dueAt EXCEPT ![g] = clock + LeaseHours]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, pinned>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < DayEnd
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<allocOf, tableOf, dueAt, pinned>>

Expire(g) ==
  /\ allocOf[g] # NoSlot
  /\ (clock >= dueAt[g] \/ clock = DayEnd)
  /\ tableOf' = [tableOf EXCEPT ![allocOf[g]] = NoGuest]
  /\ allocOf' = [allocOf EXCEPT ![g] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, dueAt, pinned>>

Revoke(g) ==
  /\ allocOf[g] # NoSlot
  /\ tableOf' = [tableOf EXCEPT ![allocOf[g]] = NoGuest]
  /\ allocOf' = [allocOf EXCEPT ![g] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, dueAt, pinned>>

Pin(s) ==
  /\ s \notin pinned
  /\ tableOf[s] = NoGuest
  /\ pinned' = pinned \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, allocOf, tableOf, dueAt>>

Unpin(s) ==
  /\ s \in pinned
  /\ pinned' = pinned \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, allocOf, tableOf, dueAt>>

Next ==
  \/ \E g \in Guests, s \in Slots : Allocate(g, s)
  \/ \E g \in Guests : Expire(g) \/ Revoke(g)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Pin(s) \/ Unpin(s)
  \/ Tick

SlotComesBack == \A g \in Guests : (allocOf[g] # NoSlot) ~> (allocOf[g] = NoSlot)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Tick) /\ WF_vars(Expire(GuestOne)) /\ WF_vars(Expire(GuestTwo))
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  GuestOne = guest1
  GuestTwo = guest2
  Slots = {slotA, slotB}
  NoSlot = noslot
  NoGuest = noguest
  LeaseHours = 2
  DayEnd = 3
INVARIANT TableMirrorsAllocations
PROPERTY SlotComesBack
nl:
The Halden smart lock keeps a small, fixed number of guest credential slots in its memory. Each slot can carry one guest's code and no more: allocating the same slot to two guests would mean either guest's code opening under the other's identity in the audit trail, and either revocation wiping out the wrong person's access. So a slot belongs to at most one guest, and the lock's slot table and the guests' own allocation records have to agree with each other exactly -- the guest that a slot's table entry names must be a guest whose allocation points back at that same slot.

Guest access is handed out as a lease, not as a permanent grant. When a guest is allocated a free slot, the allocation is stamped to expire a fixed number of hub-clock hours later. There is no revocation handshake with the guest's phone: the hub clock simply passes the expiry and the allocation is over. The hub then clears the guest's allocation and frees the slot in the table together, so the slot goes back into circulation and can be allocated to somebody else. The hub also clears everything out at the end of the day, so no allocation survives a day boundary.

The householder has a privileged override on top of the lease scheme. She can revoke a guest's allocation immediately, without waiting for the expiry, which frees the slot the same way. She can also pin a free slot, reserving it for the household's own use so that no guest is allocated it, and later unpin it to put it back into the guest pool. A pinned slot is never allocated to a guest, and she can only pin a slot that is free.

The full action set is: Allocate (a guest with no allocation is given a free, unpinned slot, stamped to expire a fixed number of hours ahead), Tick (the hub clock advances by one hour, up to the end of the day), Expire (the hub clears a guest's allocation and frees its slot once the clock has reached the expiry, or once the clock reaches the end of the day), Revoke (the householder immediately clears a guest's allocation and frees its slot), Pin (the householder reserves a free slot so that it cannot be allocated to a guest), Unpin (the householder returns a pinned slot to the guest pool).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The lock's slot table and the guests' allocations agree exactly in both directions -- a guest's allocated slot names that guest in the table and a slot's named guest points back at that slot -- so no slot is ever allocated to two guests, and no pinned slot carries a guest at all.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No guest allocation lasts forever -- every slot allocated to a guest is eventually released back into the pool, because the hub clock always reaches the allocation's expiry or the end of the day.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m2p5t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Locks, Undecided, Unvoted

VARIABLES roster, phase, ballot, verdict, burned

vars == <<roster, phase, ballot, verdict, burned>>

\* Two-phase commit over a roster that only changes while the hub is idle.
\* Burning the master secret is one-shot hardware, so it must happen only under
\* a recorded commit, and a commit only with every roster vote in favour.

TypeOK ==
  /\ roster \subseteq Locks
  /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting", "decided"}
  /\ ballot \in [Locks -> {"yes", "no", Unvoted}]
  /\ verdict \in {"commit", "abort", Undecided}
  /\ burned \subseteq Locks

BurnIsAgreed ==
  /\ (verdict = "commit") => \A l \in roster : ballot[l] = "yes"
  /\ \A l \in burned : verdict = "commit" /\ l \in roster

Init ==
  /\ roster = {}
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ ballot = [l \in Locks |-> Unvoted]
  /\ verdict = Undecided
  /\ burned = {}

Join(l) ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ l \notin roster
  /\ roster' = roster \cup {l}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, verdict, burned>>

Leave(l) ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ l \in roster
  /\ roster' = roster \ {l}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, verdict, burned>>

OpenVote ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ roster # {}
  /\ phase' = "voting"
  /\ ballot' = [l \in Locks |-> Unvoted]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, verdict, burned>>

CastVote(l, v) ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ l \in roster
  /\ ballot[l] = Unvoted
  /\ v \in {"yes", "no"}
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![l] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, phase, verdict, burned>>

Decide ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ \A l \in roster : ballot[l] # Unvoted
  /\ verdict' = IF \A l \in roster : ballot[l] = "yes" THEN "commit" ELSE "abort"
  /\ phase' = "decided"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, ballot, burned>>

Burn(l) ==
  /\ verdict = "commit"
  /\ l \in roster
  /\ l \notin burned
  /\ burned' = burned \cup {l}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, phase, ballot, verdict>>

Reset ==
  /\ verdict = "abort"
  /\ phase = "decided"
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ verdict' = Undecided
  /\ ballot' = [l \in Locks |-> Unvoted]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, burned>>

Next ==
  \/ \E l \in Locks : Join(l) \/ Leave(l) \/ Burn(l)
  \/ \E l \in Locks, v \in {"yes", "no"} : CastVote(l, v)
  \/ OpenVote
  \/ Decide
  \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Locks = {front, back, garage}
  Undecided = undecided
  Unvoted = unvoted
INVARIANT BurnIsAgreed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A Halden household occasionally performs a master re-key: every lock in the mesh burns a new master secret into its secure element and the old household keys stop working everywhere. Burning the new secret is irreversible -- the element is one-shot, the old secret is gone, and a lock that burned while the rest of the house did not would be locked out of the household for good. A lock must therefore burn at most once, and only under a decision the whole mesh actually agreed to.

The hub runs the re-key as a two-phase commit. In the first phase the hub opens a vote and every lock on the current roster votes yes or no -- yes if its battery is above the burn threshold and its secure element reports ready, no otherwise. When every lock on the roster has voted, the hub decides: commit if every single roster vote was yes, abort otherwise. In the second phase, and only if the decision was commit, each roster lock burns the new secret. A lock burns once and is then done.

The roster is not fixed, because the mesh's membership changes at runtime: locks are added when the household fits a new door and dropped when one is taken off the mesh. Membership only changes while the hub is idle -- between rounds, never during a vote and never after a decision has been reached, because a lock that joined halfway through would never have voted and a lock that left would leave a vote on the books for a participant that is no longer there.

An aborted round is not the end of the matter: the hub resets, membership can change again, and a fresh round can be opened. A committed round is the end of the matter -- there is no reset from commit, because the burn has happened.

The full action set is: Join (a lock is added to the roster while the hub is idle), Leave (a lock is dropped from the roster while the hub is idle), OpenVote (the idle hub opens a round and clears all votes, provided the roster is non-empty), CastVote (a roster lock that has not voted in this round votes yes or no), Decide (with every roster lock having voted, the hub records commit if all votes were yes and abort otherwise), Burn (a roster lock that has not yet burned burns the new master secret, permitted only under a commit decision), Reset (after an abort the hub clears the decision and the votes and returns to idle).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The hub only ever records a commit decision when every lock on the current roster voted yes, and every lock that has burned the new master secret is a lock on the current roster burning under a recorded commit decision.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m6p1t1 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Apps, NoApp, NoEdit, LeaseHours, DayEnd, RevBudget

VARIABLES clock, tenant, until, revision, author, mesh

vars == <<clock, tenant, until, revision, author, mesh>>

\* The editing lease dies by clock, not by agreement, and the mesh reorders, so
\* the hub re-checks the stamped revision on arrival. The authorship trail is
\* what makes a silently overwritten edit impossible to hide.

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in 0..DayEnd
  /\ tenant \in Apps \cup {NoApp}
  /\ until \in 0..(DayEnd + LeaseHours)
  /\ revision \in 0..RevBudget
  /\ author \in [0..RevBudget -> Apps \cup {NoApp}]
  /\ mesh \in [Apps -> (0..RevBudget) \cup {NoEdit}]

LeaseLive == tenant # NoApp /\ clock < until

EveryRevisionAuthored ==
  \A i \in 0..RevBudget : (author[i] # NoApp) <=> (i < revision)

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ tenant = NoApp
  /\ until = 0
  /\ revision = 0
  /\ author = [i \in 0..RevBudget |-> NoApp]
  /\ mesh = [a \in Apps |-> NoEdit]

GrantLease(a) ==
  /\ ~LeaseLive
  /\ tenant = NoApp
  /\ tenant' = a
  /\ until' = clock + LeaseHours
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, revision, author, mesh>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < DayEnd
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tenant, until, revision, author, mesh>>

Reclaim ==
  /\ tenant # NoApp
  /\ (clock >= until \/ clock = DayEnd)
  /\ tenant' = NoApp
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, until, revision, author, mesh>>

Compose(a) ==
  /\ tenant = a
  /\ LeaseLive
  /\ mesh[a] = NoEdit
  /\ mesh' = [mesh EXCEPT ![a] = revision]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, tenant, until, revision, author>>

Accept(a) ==
  /\ mesh[a] # NoEdit
  /\ mesh[a] = revision
  /\ tenant = a
  /\ LeaseLive
  /\ revision < RevBudget
  /\ author' = [author EXCEPT ![revision] = a]
  /\ revision' = revision + 1
  /\ mesh' = [mesh EXCEPT ![a] = NoEdit]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, tenant, until>>

Reject(a) ==
  /\ mesh[a] # NoEdit
  /\ (mesh[a] # revision \/ tenant # a \/ ~LeaseLive \/ revision = RevBudget)
  /\ mesh' = [mesh EXCEPT ![a] = NoEdit]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, tenant, until, revision, author>>

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Apps : GrantLease(a) \/ Compose(a) \/ Accept(a) \/ Reject(a)
  \/ Tick
  \/ Reclaim

LeaseAlwaysReturns == (tenant # NoApp) ~> (tenant = NoApp)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Tick) /\ WF_vars(Reclaim)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Apps = {phone, tablet}
  NoApp = noapp
  NoEdit = noedit
  LeaseHours = 2
  DayEnd = 3
  RevBudget = 2
INVARIANT EveryRevisionAuthored
PROPERTY LeaseAlwaysReturns
nl:
The Halden hub keeps one access-code list for the whole house, and it is the record every lock reads from. The list is revised in place: each accepted edit moves it from one revision to the next, and the hub keeps, for each revision it has passed through, the name of the companion app whose edit produced it. That authorship trail is the operator's guarantee against a lost update: there must be an author recorded for every revision the list has actually passed through, and no author recorded for revisions it has not reached yet. A revision with no author would mean an edit was overwritten by another without anybody noticing.

Only one app at a time may edit, and the right to edit is leased. The hub grants the editing lease to an app when no live lease is outstanding, stamped to expire a fixed number of hub-clock hours ahead. Leases are not handed back by agreement; the clock passes the expiry and the lease is dead, which is what stops a phone that has gone out of range from freezing the household's access list for the rest of the day. Once a lease is dead the hub reclaims it and the next app can take it. At the end of the day the hub reclaims the lease regardless.

Edits do not arrive instantly. An app with a live lease composes an edit against the revision it can currently see and puts it on the home mesh, which delivers with arbitrary delay and in arbitrary order -- an edit composed early can easily arrive after one composed later. So the hub checks on arrival: it accepts an edit only if the revision the edit was composed against is still the list's current revision and the composing app's lease is still live. On acceptance the composing app is recorded as the author of the revision that has just been superseded and the list moves on by one. An edit composed against a superseded revision, or by an app whose lease has since died, is rejected outright, and so is any edit that arrives once the day's revision budget is spent. Each app keeps at most one edit on the mesh at a time.

The full action set is: GrantLease (an app takes the editing lease when no live lease is outstanding, stamped to expire a fixed number of hours ahead), Tick (the hub clock advances by one hour, up to the end of the day), Reclaim (the hub takes back a lease whose expiry the clock has passed, or any lease once the clock reaches the end of the day), Compose (an app holding a live lease and with nothing already on the mesh puts an edit on the mesh stamped with the revision it can currently see), Accept (the hub takes an edit off the mesh and applies it, recording the composing app as the author of the superseded revision and advancing the list, permitted only if the stamped revision is still current, the composer's lease is still live and the day's revision budget is not spent), Reject (the hub throws away an edit whose stamped revision is superseded, whose composer's lease has died, or which arrives after the revision budget is spent).

SAFETY PROPERTY: An author is recorded for exactly those revisions the access list has already passed through and for no others, so every revision transition is attributable to one accepted edit and no edit has been overwritten unrecorded.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The editing lease never sticks -- an app that holds the lease always eventually loses it, because the hub clock reaches the expiry or the end of the day and the hub reclaims it.
